hearings.judge: CCH23 XXV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Advocate for Dhr filed memo along with copy of the order passed by the Hon\''ble Supreme Court in Appeal No.25339/2023. Perused the said order. On perusal of the same, it appears that the Hon\''ble Supreme Court has granted time to the Jdr to vacate and handover the vacant possession of petition schedule property till March 2024. Jdr is present. Sri. R.V.K advocate filed vakalath for Jdr. Advocate for Jdr filed memo, stating that Jdr is handing over the keys of the suit schedule premises to the decree holder by reserving his right to initiate separate proceedings against the Dhr for recovery of security deposits if any. Memo is placed on record. Counsel for Dhr has received the key of the petition schedule property from the Jdr and made an endorsement for having received the key. Since, the Jdr has handed over the key of the petition schedule property, I feel it is just and proper to close the petitioner as E.F.S, in view of this, I proceed to pass the following:- ORDER Petition is ordered to be closed as E.F.S.

hearings.judge: CCH23 XXV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Perused the bailiff report. As per bailiff report petitioner schedule property was kept under lock. As such delivery warrant is not executed. Advocate for Dhr filed IA.No.1 U/s 151 of CPC seeking for an order for issue of delivery warrant by break open the lock of the petition schedule property. Heard and perused the affidavit in support of application. The grounds urged in the affidavit are satisfied to issue delivery warrant by break open the lock. In view of this, and in the interest of justice, I proceed to pass the following:- ORDER IA.No.1 is allowed. Accordingly, issue delivery warrant by break open the lock. R/by 06.04.2024.

hearings.judge: CCH23 XXV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Perused the office note. As per office note RFA.No.140/2019 is pending. Perused the record. The Dhr has produced the copy of the order passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.140/2019. On perusal of the said order, it is clear that the said R.F.A was disposed of on 11.08.2023 by confirming the judgment and decree passed by this court. Thus, directing the respondent i.e., Jdr herein to vacate and hand over the vacant possession of the schedule premises within 2 months from the date of receipt of copy of the judgment. This execution petition is filed within 2 years from the date of judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.140/2019. Hence, issuance of cause notice to the Jdr is hereby dispensed with. Accordingly, issue delivery warrant against the Jdr. R/by 23.02.2024.

hearings.judge: CCH33 XXXIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Learned counsel for DHr present. The present Execution Petition is filed seeking to issue delivery warrant in respect of decreetal schedule property stated in Execution Petition. The O.S. 8424/2017 filed by the plaintiffs came to be decreed as per judgment dtd 4.10.2023. Till this date, no appeal is preferred against the judgment and decree passed by this Court. As per order 21 Rule 22 of CPC, where an application for execution is made, within two years of the date of the decree, the Court need not issue notice to the person against whom execution is applied for requiring him to show-cause. In the case of hand, the present execution is filed within two years of date of decree. Hence, cause notice need not be issued to the Jdrs. Further, no appeal is preferred against the judgment and decree passed by this Court. Hence, issue delivery warrant in respect of execution schedule property as prayed in the Execution Petition. R/by 3.2.2024.

hearings.business_text: Taken up before the Lok-Adalalath. Decree-holder and Judgment-debtor No.1 to 4 are present along with their respective counsels. After conciliation both parties have agreed for settlement and files compromise petition. The contents of compromise are admitted by the parties. As per the terms of the compromise they have mutually fixed the value of the schedule property as to Rs.70 Lakhs. Judgment-debtor No.2 L N Maruthesh has agreed to purchase the shares of Decree-holder, Judgment-debtor No.1, 3 and 4. They have acknowledge the receipts of Dds. The compromise is lawful. Accordingly, the compromise petition is accepted. Judgment-debtor No.2 is the owner of entire petition schedule property and he is also residing in the schedule premises. Judgment-debtor No.2 is liberty to obtain sale deed in respect of Decree-holder and Judgment-debtors No.1, 3 and 4 through court. Accordingly, execution petition is settled in terms of compromise and closed. Office is directed to return the court commissioner fee of Rs.10,000/- deposited on 23-07-2024 in favour of Sri.N V Nagesh, Advocate Roll No. KAR 2808/2011.

hearings.business_text: The case is taken up on Board as per the advance application I.A.No.2 filed by the Jdr.No.2 counsel. The counsel for Jdr.No.2 files I.A.No.3 under Order XXI rule 69 CPC to adjourn and stoppage of sale proceedings fixed today i.e., on 17-08-2024. The counsel for Jdr.No.2 submitted that he has made a proposal for settlement, the RFA is pending before Hon\''ble High Court filed by him challenging the preliminary decree and he prays time by adjourning the auction of property. The counsel for Dhr. Opposed the applications and submitted that Jdr.No.2 has not challenged the order on FDP, RFA is not pending, Jdr.No.2 has got opportunity to participate in the auction and to purchase the property and prayed for dismissal. After considering the submissions of both sides, the record disclose that Decree holder filed the petition based on final decree in FDP No.158/2022 dated 07-10-2023, wherein the Court has ordered for auction of decreetal property with permission to parities to participate in the auction in purchase of property. The counsel for Jdr.No.2 has admitted that he has not challenged the order of FDP. The Execution Petition is filed based on final decree. The Executing Court cannot go beyond the final decree. The grounds stated in the applications that the Jdr.No.2 intend to secure the witness to the Will and made application before Hon\''ble High Court for restoration of MFA No.1723/2022. Since there is no stay regarding proceedings of this petition, the Court has already ordered for auction of decreetal properties and fixed first and second bid on this day i.e., on 17-08-2024, at this time, there is no ground the stoppage of sale. Accordingly, I.A.No.3 is rejected. [S. NATARAJ] VI ACC & SJ., B\''LURU CITY Await for Commissioner report. Call on 31-08-2024.

hearings.judge: CCH43 XLII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: This EP is filed by DHR to enforce the order passed by KRERA in Complaint No.CMP/UR/220629/0000969 dated: 25.05.2023. In EP the amount sought is Rs.79,83,389/- and also possession of the schedule property and execution of the registered sale deed in favour of the DHR. JDR filed objection to main petition stating that Civil court has no jurisdiction to execute the order passed by the KRERA. The KRERA has not followed the due procedure while passing the impugned order. So, it prayed to dismiss the petition with cost. Heard both side on maintainability of the EP. Perused the materials on record. Counsel for DHR produced Order passed by KRERA dated: 24.08.2023 which discloses that the present DHR has filed application for transfer of the EP to City Civil Court and accordingly it was transferred to this court for execution. But, KRERA has not passed considered order stating that it is unable to execute the order. So, as per Rule 26 of KRERA the Authority itself has got jurisdiction to execute its order. But, in this case authority has not given any reasons for transfer of the order to Civil Court for execution of the same. The citation relied by the JDR in WP No.17821/2025 clubbed with WP 18348/2025 and WP 19184/2025 dated: 31.10.2025 Mantri Developer Pvt Ltd., Vs. Sunil Veetil is directly applicable to the facts of this case. In said case the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka by considering the judgment of Hon’ble Apex Court was pleased to hold that Civil Court has no jurisdiction to execute the order passed by the KRERA as the said order does not fall under the definition of decree-Sec.2(2) of the CPC. covered under the definition of decree. Therefore, the appropriate remedy available to the DHR is to approach KRERA itself and seek for execution of the order passed by it in Complaint No.CMP/UR/220629/0000969 dated: 25.05.2023. Accordingly, this EP is dismissed as not at all maintainable before Civil Court.

hearings.judge: CCH43 XLII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Counsel for the JDR is present. Heard reply from advocate for DHR. As per Sec.40(1) of RERA Act the order passed by RERA Authority can be executed as if it is a land revenue. As per (2) of Sec.40 the order can be executed by following the procedure prescribed under Rule 26 of RERA Rules. As per Rule 26 the RERA Authority itself may execute the order by following the procedure as if it were a decree and the event of its inability to execute the order, then it can send the order to the Civil Court for execution. In the letter dated: 22.09.2023 written by Registrar, RERA it is stated that the order is passed on 24.08.2023. But said order is not produced by the DHR. Hence, DHR shall produce the said order for reference in this EP, advocate for DHR prays time, time is granted. Call on 05-06-2026.

hearings.judge: CCH19 VII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSINS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The learned counsel for the DHr has filed I.A.No.4 u/s 151 of CPC and sought to direct the office to release the the sale amount of movables Rs.35,000/- in favour of the DHr. The said application is supported by the affidavit of DHr, wherein it is stated that the JDr has left certain movable properties in the execution schedule properties and the same were sold in auction and the sale proceeds of Rs.35,000/- was deposited by the Bailiff into the Court. The DHr is also sought for recovery of Rs.3,85,545/- and hence prayed to release the said sale proceeds in favour of the DHr. I have perused the order sheet, the DHr has also sought for recovery of Rs.3,85,545/- in addition to the delivery of possession as per the Judgment and Decree passed by this Court in O.S No.3888/2022. The delivery of possession was executed by breaking open the lock as per the order of this Court dated 19.06.2024. After delivery of execution schedule property into the hands of DHr, it was reported that JDr has left certain movables in the Execution schedule premises. The same was ordered to be sold in auction vide order dated 30.08.2024. As per the said order, auction was conducted and Rs.35,000/- was deposited into the Court. Considering all the above said facts and circumstances, I proceed to pass the following ORDER I.A.No.4 filed U/s 151 of CPC is hereby allowed. Office is directed to release the amount of Rs.35,000/- deposited by the Bailiff in R.O No.2089/2024 dated 08.11.2024 in favour of the DHr. The DHr shall adjust such Rs.35,000/- towards the Decretal amount. Steps by 16.01.2025.

hearings.judge: CCH19 VII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSINS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: As per the Order dated 30.08.2024, movable properties found in the Decree schedule property was sold in Auction for Rs.35,000/- by the Bailiff of this Court. Such sale of movable properties by the Bailiff is hereby accepted. The demand draft for Rs.35,000/- shall be taken into credit of the concerned Account by the office. The learned counsel for the DHr submits that apart from Delivery warrant, DHr is also sought for recovery of Rs.3,85,545/- as per the Decree and paid for taking steps. Call on 27.11.2024.

hearings.judge: CCH19 VII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSINS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: heard the learned counsel for the DHr on I.A.No.3. It is prayed in the I.A.No.3 to issue Warrant of Sale of Movables Item No.1 to 11 by way of Auction. The said application is annexed with the affidavit of the DHr, wherein it is stated that as per the Decree passed in O.S 3888/2022, vacant possession of the execution schedule premises was handed over to the DHr, but in the Decree schedule property there were about 11 properties and the same was given to the possession of DHr and the same is kept in the premises of the Decree schedule property and prayed for conducting the sale of such property. I have perused the report of the Court Ameen wherein it is stated that on 04.07.2024, the vacant possession of the suit schedule property was handed over to the DHr. In the said premises there were 11 movable properties worth around Rs.30000/- and inventory of the same was conducted and the same was given to the possession of the DHr. Considering the said shara and also considering the contents of I.A.No.3 and its annexed affidavit, I proceed to pass the following ORDER Office is directed to conduct the Auction Sale of the movable properties shown in the Delivery Warrant i.e., Item No.1 to 11 found in the Decree schedule property of which Inventory was done by the Ameen of the Court in accordance with law. Issue Sale Proclamation and Sale Warrant of movable properties. Office is directed to deposit the sale proceeds of such Items to the concerned Account of the Court. Call on 30.10.2024.

Heard advocate for Decree Holder on I.A.No.1 filed under Order 21 Rule 54 of CPC. Perused entire materials on record. The above petition is filed for execution of Compromise Decree dated 08.01.2024 passed in O.S.7829/2023. As the Judgment Debtor has failed to comply with the terms of Compromise Decree, the Decree Holder has filed the present petition for execution of Decree. Along with this petition, the Decree Holder has filed present application seeking attachment of immovable property of Judgment Debtor. In support of the same, the Decree Holder has produced uttara patra and Encumbrance certificate in respect of property bearing No.G1, Municipal No. 1299/33-1/G1 on the ground floor- Northern side of Manasa Residency Apartment situated at 2nd Main Road, Magadi Road, Chord Road, Ward No.36, Bangalore. On perusal of notarized copy of Uttara Patra, it is clear that the said property is standing in the name of Judgment Debtor. The Encumbrance certificate makes clear that the said property has been purchased by the husband of the Judgment Debtor. Hence, in order to provide fruits of the Decree to the Decree Holder, it is just and proper to pass the following ORDER IA.No.1 filed under Order 21 Rule 54 r/w Section 151 of CPC by the Decree Holder is hereby allowed. Issue attachment warrant against Judgment Debtor in respect of her property bearing No.G1, Municipal No. 1299/33-1/G1 on the ground floor - Northern side of Manasa Residency Apartment situated at 2nd Main Road, Magadi Road, Chord Road, Ward No.36, Bangalore which is more-fully described in the Execution petition, if PF paid. hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Heard the arguments of the L/c for the DHR on the limitation. In this case the DHR has got the decree for recovery of money on 21.06.2011. The 12 yrs limitations to file the executing the decree will expires on 21.06.2023. But this petition being filed before this court on 05.02.2024, which is after lapse of more than 7 months 15 days. But L/c for the DHR submits that, the Hon\''ble Apex court in its sue moto WP(C) no.3/20 and Misc application no.21/22 , vide its order dt 10.01.2022 excluded the period btw 15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022 for the purpose of limitation. Thus he contended that, the said period is requires to be added to the remaining period commences from 01.03.2022 to file the petition. According to him as on 01.03.2022 the DHR has 1 yr 3 months 20 days time to file the petition, for which the saved period btw 15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022, which comes of 1 yr 11 months, 13 days are added to the 1 yr ,3 months 20 days, the total period available to the DHR to file petition is 3 yrs 3 months 3 days from 01.03.2022, said period will expires on 03.07.2025. As the petition is filed on 05.02.2024 itself the said petition is well in time. The contention of the DHR is cannot be accepted for the simple reason that, the Hon\''ble Apex court by considering the gravity of the Covid break down in the country was pleased to exclude the period btw 15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022 in the event if the limitation expires btw that period or limitation commences, in any of the circumstances the Hon\''ble Apex court hold that, 90 days period is available from 01.03.2022. If the remaining period of limitation is exceeding the 90 days in that event the longer period is going to be applied. If the said aspect are considered, the case of the DHR will not fall in any of the conditions. In fact the limitation to file the present petition was not expired btw the period excluded for the purpose of limitation by the Hon\''ble Apex court. In fact the DHR was having 1 yr, 3 months 20 days period from 01.03.2022 to file their petition, which expires on 03.07.2023 in that event the DHR should have been filed the present petition on or before 03.07.2023, but its been filed on 05.02.2024, as the present petition is filed after expiry of limitation period, thus petition do not survives for the execution. Thus petition is dismissed, as the decree is time barred

hearings.business_text: Advocate for Dhr filed I.A. u/Sec.151 of the CPC in order to issue delivery warrant by break opening the lock of the suit schedule premises with the help of jurisdictional Pulakeshinagar Police in the interest of justice and equity. It was contended in the application that after the issuance of the delivery warrant with respect to schedule B and C properties the court ameen went to the spot. However, he noticed the doors of the schedule properties are locked. Therefore, he endorsed the shara stating that a specific order is to be passed by the court to lock open the breaks to hand over the possession of the schedule properties in favor of the Dhr with the help of the police. Accordingly, this application has been filed. Heard. Perused the shara endorsed by the court ameen. It is clear that since the doors are locked the court ameen cannot execute the warrant as ordered by this court by its order dated 01.08.2025. in order to satisfy the decree it is necessary to allow the application. Accordingly, I.A. filed by the Dhr u/Sec.151 of the CPC is hereby allowed. Re-issue delivery warrant with respect to schedule B and C properties, if PF paid. The court ameen is directed to break open the locks of the premises if the doors are locked. Further the jurisdictional Pulakeshinagar Police are hereby directed in order to assist the court ameen in execution of the delivery warrant. Returnable by

hearings.business_text: Advocate for Dhr filed memo along with the copy of the sale deed. Further filed process to issue delivery warrant of the suit schedule property. Process is also furnished. On perusal entire file it is clear that this court has directed the defendant to execute the sale deed with respect to schedule B and C properties in favor of the plaintiffs after accepting the balance sale consideration. Accordingly, this court by the order dated 07.07.2025 directed the Sheristedar of the court to execute the sale deed on behalf of the court. Accordingly, she has executed the sale deed on behalf of the court and copy of that document is submitted before the court. However, the possession of the schedule property is still in the hands of the defendant. Therefore, it is necessary to issue delivery warrant with respect to schedule B and C properties as claimed in the execution petition. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following : ORDER Issue delivery warrant with respect to schedule B and C properties. Returnable by

hearings.business_text: Learned Counsel for DHR files application u/s 151 CPC seeking for order of issuing of delivery warrant to break open the lock put on suit schedule property. On perusal of the order sheet it is forthcoming that on previous date of hearing this court has issued delivery warrant. The bailiff has submitted the report that the possession of the schedule property can’t be delivered to DHR as the schedule property is locked by JDR and thereby prays to issue the order to break open the lock put on the schedule property. Perused the report furnished by bailiff and affidavit of DHR. Hence at this stage this court feels expedient and interest of justice to issue delivery warrant with break open the lock put on this schedule property. The DHR in his application sought the assistance of the police to break open the lock but in the report of the bailiff it is not seen that the assistance of the police is required to execute the delivery warrant. Hence prayer for police help to execute the delivery warrant is rejected. Office to issue delivery warrant with break open the lock. Leaned counsel for DHR paid PF. Await report. Call on 30.08.2024.

hearings.judge: CCH12 XVI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called. Counsel for DHR present and files memo with details of jurisdictional police. ORDER ON IA DATED 03-08-2024. This I.A. is filed by the DHR U/S 151 of CPC seeking assisstance of jurisdictional police to the Bailiff to break open the lock for attaching movable properties of JDR. In accompanying affidavit to the I.A. it is stated by DHR that the JDR and his nieghbours and his family members did not allow them to their house by not opening the door for attaching movables of JDR intentionally and further they are making threats and creating fear and obstruct for execution of attachment of immovable property. On perusal of counter copy of previous warrant of attachment of movables the bailiff requested for police aid as the father of JDR obstructed him. The learned Counsel for DHR files a memo with details of jurisdictional police as the Thilak nagar Police Station. If this application is allowed will not cause hardship to other side as the police shall aid to break open with peacefull manner without disturbing anybody in the location of JDR. Hence, this Court proceed to pass the following ORDER I.A. filed by the DHR U/S 151 of CPC for assisstance of jurisdictional police is hereby allowed. Consequently, the concerned police officer of Thilak nagar Police Station is hereby directed to give aid to the bailiff to break open the lock for attaching movable properties of JDR in the address mentioned in this petition in peacefull manner without disturbing the public. Re-issue attachment warrant of movables with police help.

hearings.business_text: Counsel for decree holders is present and prays time.In judgment passed by Honble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642 of 2025 in case of Peruyammal (Dead Through Lrs.) Vs V. Rajamani and another etc., dated 06.03.2025, it is held that, The executing court must dispose of the execution proceedings within six months from the date of filing, which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay. In view of above said judgment, the decree holders has not taken effective steps. Prayer of Counsel for decree-holders is rejected. There are no grounds to proceed further. Hence, this petition is dismissed as non prosecution.

hearings.business_text: Learned Counsel for Decree Holder submits that no cause notice on execution petition is needed to be served on Jdr., as it is filed within 2 years from the date of decree passed in suit and he requested for an order to dispense with notice to Jdr., in the interest of justice and equity. 02. O.S. No.5034/2019 was decreed on 19.12.2023 and the defendants has not paid the decreetal amount nor handed over the possession of the property to the DHR. 03. The Dhr., has filed the execution petition within 2 years from the date of that order. Order 21 Rule 22(2) of CPC gives the discretionary power to the court to dispense with notice contemplated by the order 21 Rule 22 (a) (b) (c), if it finds that issue of such notice would cause unreasonable delay and would defeat the the ends of justice. 04. Dhr., has made out the grounds to consider their plea. Issuance of notice to Jdr., would cause unreasonable delay in giving relief to the party who has sought for recovery of possession of the property and decreetal amount. Hence, following order. :: ORDER :: Acting under Order XXI Rule 22 R/w Sec 151 of CPC issuance of show cause notice to Jdr. is hereby dispensed with. Issue A/W/M against JDR for recovery of decreetal amount. Issue delivery warrant if P.F., is paid. Call on 16.04.2024.

DHR counsel filed I.A No.3 U/s.151 of CPC and submitted that Sub-Registrar, in order to register court Sale Deed insisting to produce E-Katha.’ Hence, DHR counsel prays to direct the Sub-Registrar to register the court Sale Deed by accepting the available draft E-Katha by exempting the E-Katha. There is some force in the submission of the learned counsel for DHR. This execution petition filed in order to execute the decree dt:01.12.2023 passed in O.S No.3485/2018. Since, the JDR is not come forward to execute the Sale Deed in terms of Decree, this court constrained to appoint the Court Commissioner so as to execute the Sale deed. Usually E-Katha can be made by the owner of the property. But, in the present case JDR has not come forward to execute the Sale Deed. Hence, this court appointed Court Commissioner in order to execute the Decree. Under such circumstances it is not possible to change E-Katha for Registration of the Sale deed. Hence, I.A No.3 filed U/s.151 of CPC is allowed. It is hereby directed to Sub-Registrar to register the court Sale Deed by accepting the available draft E-Katha by exempting the E-Katha. hearings.business_text: Case called out. DHR counsel present. I heard the arguments on I.A No.2 on the side of counsel for DHR. I.A No.2 filed U/o 26 Rule 10(c) of CPC praying to appoint the Sheristedar/ Court official as court Commissioner to present the documents and to execute Sale Deed for Registration in terms of the Decree. In the affidavit filed in support of I.A No.2, the DHR sworn that this Execution petition filed against JDR for execution of Decree but, the JDR has failed to execute Registered Sale Deed in favour of DHR in respect of schedule property. Hence, it is necessary to appoint Sheristedar/ Court official as court Commissioner to execute and Register Sale deed on behalf of this court. It is sworn that the DHR is ready to pay the Commissioner fee. The learned counsel for DHR submitted that DHR already deposited balance amount of Rs.45,00,000/- before this court on 27.02.2025 by way of D.D. I heard on side of learned counsel for DHR and perused the entire records. On perusal of records, it would go to show that since cause notice not served to JDR. Notice was served by way of substituted service of paper publication in Samyuktha Karnataka daily news paper dt:23.07.2025 which is held sufficient, but JDR not appeared before the court. This court passed Judgment and Decree in O.S No.3485/2018 and directed the defendant to execute Registered Sale Deed with respect to the plaint schedule property in favour of the plaintiff in terms of the Sale Agreement dt: 22.05.2015 by receiving balance Sale consideration amount within two months from the date of the Judgment and also directed to handover the possession of the plaint schedule property to the plaintiff by executing the Sale Deed. It is ordered that in case the defendant fails to execute the Sale deed the plaintiff is entitled to get the Sale Deed through the process of the court by depositing balance Sale consideration amount in the court. The JDR failed to execute the Registered Sale Deed in favour of DHR by receiving balance consideration amount. DHR already deposited balance consideration amount of Rs.45,00,000/- before this court. The Jdr is liberty to withdraw that Sale consideration amount. Hence, there is sufficient grounds made out by the DHR to appoint Sheristedar/ Court official as court Commissioner to present the documents and to execute Sale Deed for Registration in terms of the Decree. Hence, I.A No.2 filed U/o 26 Rule 10(c) of CPC is hereby Allowed. It is requested to Registrar, City Civil Court, Bengaluru to name and depute any of the Sheristedar/ Court official as court Commissioner. DHR counsel prays to furnish draft Sale Deed. Call for Draft Sale Deed by 26.09.2025.

hearings.business_text: Case called at 4.53 pm. Counsel appearing for the DHR is absent. Perused the contents of the petition, IA.No.I and affidavit. The decree under execution was passed in OS.No.1053/2009 dated:25.11.2010. The DHR has also filed IA.No.I under Sec.5 of the Limitation Act. In the affidavit filed in support of the application the DHR has stated that due to amalgamation of DHR bank and Covid-19 pandemic the DHR could not file the application. As per Sec.3 of Limitation Act every application filed after prescribed period of limitation shall be dismissed. As per Article 136 of Limitation Act 1963 for execution of any decree or order of any Civil Court the period of limitation is 12 years. Hence, the present petition is barred by law of limitation. Accordingly, IA.No.I and petition filed by the DHR is dismissed as barred by law of limitation.

hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Heard the arguments of the L/c for the DHR on the limitation. In this case the DHR has got the decree for recovery of money on 24.07.2008. The 12 yrs limitations to file the executing the decree will expires on 24.07.2020. But this petition being filed before this court on 15.03.2024, which is after lapse of more than 1 year, 7 months 22 days. But L/c for the DHR submits that, the Hon'ble Apex court in its sue moto WP(C) no.3/20 and Misc application no.21/22 , vide its order dt 10.01.2022 excluded the period btw 15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022 for the purpose of computing the limitation for all purpose for filing all kinds of dispute, thus the said period is requires to be excluded. Off course, the DHR is right that, if at all the limitation to file the petition is expires during the above said period, from 01.03.2022 the DHR would get 90 days time period to file the present petition, it means to say the DHR ought to have filed the present petition on or before 31.05.2022, but filed the present petition after expiry of the said period. Thus the petition is filed after expiry of limitation period, which deserves to be dismissed.

judge: 13-CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Heard the arguments of the L/c for the DHR on the limitation. In this case the DHR has got the decree for recovery of money on 27.10.2010. The 12 yrs limitations to file the executing the decree will expires on 27.10.2022. But this petition being filed before this court on 15.03.2024, which is after lapse of more than 1 year, 4 months 19 days. But L/c for the DHR submits that, the Hon'ble Apex court in its sue moto WP(C) no.3/20 and Misc application no.21/22 , vide its order dt 10.01.2022 excluded the period btw 15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022 for the purpose of computing the limitation for all purpose for filing all kinds of dispute, thus the said period is requires to be excluded. Off course, the DHR is right that, if at all the limitation to file the petition is expires during the above said period, from 01.03.2022 the DHR would get 90 days time period to file the present petition, but in this case, the limitation was not expired during the period excluded in the above said order of the Apex Court. In fact even after expiry of said period, the DHR had the limitation to file the present petition, which was not filed. But it is not the case of the DHR that the period excluded in the above said order is requires to be added as period the DHR had to file the present petition. Thus this court is of the opinion the DHR ought to have filed his petition on or before 27.10.2022, as the same is filed after expiry of 12 yrs, thus same is deserves to be dismissed. Accordingly dismissed as barred by time.

hearings.judge: CCH12 XVI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The counsel for DHR filed a memo on 29.06.2024 stating that this execution is filed within 2 years. In original suit it was decreed exparte. Hence, notice is not necessary to the decree holder as this execution petition is filed within 2 years. Hence, prayed to dispense with the notice. This court presume on the above memo that, the DHR wrongly mentioned as notice to decree holder. But it is for notice to judgment debtor. In support of his memo, he has filed judgment in Vasanth Rao Vs. Raj Reddy dt. 02.12.2002 in AIR 2003 (NOC) 600 (AP) and submitted that in this citation the Hon\''ble High Court of AP dispense the issuance of notice to JDR. But, on perusal of the same citation it’s para no.7, it is opined by Hon’ble Justice that, “It does not mean that notice to the respondent is totally prohibited in all cases where the execution petition is filed within 2 years. I am of the view that even in such cases it is always open for the executing court, in exercise of it’s discretion to issue notice to meet the ends of justice. Where such discretion is judiciously exercise and particularly where reasons are recorded, it cannot be said that there is any error in the exercise of jurisdiction vested under law”. And finally the Hon\''ble High Court dismissed the said Civil Revision Petition. Now this court gone through the judgment and decree in O.S. No. 3218/2019 which is the executable decree under this petition. It is true that, that case is disposed on 27.02.2023 and this execution petition filed on 16.03.2024 which is within 2 years from the passing of that decree. But, in operative portion of the said judgment, it is clearly ordered as, “The defendant is hereby directed to execute the absolute sale deed in favour of Plaintiff in pursuance of the sale agreement dt. 20.07.2016 by receiving the balance sale consideration amount of Rs. 25 Lakh and hand over possession of the suit schedule property in favour of the Plaintiff. “In the event of defendant’s failure to execute and register the sale deed in favour of Plaintiff, the Plaintiff is at liberty to get sale deed through process of law”. Next to that, on perusal of the execution petition the first prayer is “direct the defendant to execute the absolute sale deed in favour of the decree holder”. Hence, it is clear that as the direction sought against the JDR to execute the sale deed and the execution of sale deed through court of law is subsequent one then it is necessary to issue notice to the defendant / JDR to execute the sale deed as per judgment and decree. Therefore, as per facts and circumstances of the case and above discussion this court is of the considered opinion that, the issuance of cause notice to JDR is very necessary. Hence, proceed to pass the following; ORDER The memo dt. 29.06.2024 filed by the DHR is hereby rejected. Issue cause notice to JDR through court and RPAD and the counsel for JDR directed to pay PF in the office. Call on 31.08.2024.

hearings.business_text: On 19.06.2024 the counsel for the DHR has filed a memo stating that the DHRs have taken possession on 05.06.2024 of the suit schedule property as per the Delivery warrant issued by this Court and accordingly they prayed to close the execution petition. Before accepting the said memo dated 19.06.2024, the DHR has comeup with a fresh memo dated 07.11.2024 stating that due to subsequent appearance of the JDRs and also owing to the subsequent developments in the instant case, they have decided to proceed with the execution petition in respect of arrears of rent due and payable by the JDRs as per the Judgment and Decree in O.S.2503/2020. The JDRs have not filed any objections to the said applications. The 2nd memo dated 07.11.2024 was filed even before accepting the 1st memo. According to the DHR, they are entitled to the arrears of rent. Hence, considering the fact that the 2nd memo is filed before the acceptance of the 1st memo and the DHR being the dominoes litus, this court is of the considered opinion that the the DHR shall be permitted to withdraw the 1st memo, thus the 2nd memo dated 07.11.2024 shall be accepted. Accordingly, the memo dated 07.11.2024 filed by the DHR is hereby accepted and the DHR is permitted to proceed with the petition in accordance with law. For further steps by 21.04.2025

hearings.judge: CCH16 XVII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Both the counsels present. Counsel for Dhr filed memo for withdrawal of the petition. Perused the memo in detail. As mentioned therein, the Dhr has filed O.S No.8882/2019 for partition and separate possession and it was decreed on 16-01-2023. Pursuant thereto present petition has been filed for enforcement of decree. After his appearance Jdr raised plea of maintainability of petition without exhausting the final decree proceedings. Hence, Dhr seeking permission of the court to withdraw the petition with liberty to institute final decree proceedings. The Jdr has not raised any objections to the memo. It is apparent that after obtaining preliminary decree for partition in O.S No.8882/2019, the plaintiff/Dhr instead of filing final decree proceedings has mistakenly filed the present execution petition. The mistakes should not defeat the ends of justice. Wherefore, memo is accepted. In the result, Dhr is permitted to withdraw the present petition with liberty to file final decree proceedings as prayed in the memo.

hearings.business_text: ORDER ON MEMO OF CALCULATION Learned counsel for DHR files memo of calculation showing the balance amount to be payable by the JDR, along with documents. Learned counsel for DHR has filed the objection along with documents and prays for not to consider the objections of JDR. Heard on both side. Learned counsel for JDR submits that as per the account statements details furnished by him, he has paid an entire EP amount and he paid excess amount of Rs.58,217/- and further he submits that there is no amount to be payable to DHR by JDR. On perusal of the records it is forthcoming that the suit has been filed on 06.06.2019 and the same was decreed on 03.06.2023. If he had paid any amount as alleged by him the court would have considered the said payment and it would have deducted the said amount in the main amount claimed by the DHR and decree would have been passed for the remaining amount. No documents are forthcoming from JDR showing the challenge of the decree passed in O.S.No.4001/2019. Further on perusal of the account statement furnished by the JDR it discloses that whatever account statement furnished by JDR not pertaining to the JDR in the present case, hence the contention of the JDR with respect to the payment of excess amount of Rs.58,217/- do not survive for consideration. Hence memo of calculation furnished by DHR is considered. DHR is permitted to proceed against JDR to recover the balance amount. For steps to realization of the balance EP amount. Call on 19.12.2025.

hearings.judge: CCH35 XXXIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called out. Counsel for DHR twice called out, absent. On the last date of hearing, this court had directed to the counsel for Dhr to taken steps against Jdr No.1 and 2. However, despite the repeated and final opportunities and lapse of considerable time, the decree-holder has failed to appear and prosecute the execution petition diligently. It is relevant to refer to the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs and Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani and Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025, directed all High Courts to ensure that pending execution petitions are disposed of within a period of six months. In view of the long pendency of this execution petition, failure of the decree-holder to take any effective steps and in light of the directions of the Hon’ble Apex Court and the High Court circular, this Court finds no reason to keep this execution petition pending any further. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non-prosecution. The decree-holder is at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law. Office is directed to return the copy of decree to the counsel for DHR upon verification and identification.

Rajamani & Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640–3642/2025, dated 06.03.2025, and Circular No. 2/2025 dated 01.04.2025 issued by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka mandating disposal of execution petitions within six months, this Court is duty bound to prevent unnecessary delay and ensure expeditious disposal of execution petitions.  For steps against Jdr No.1 and 2 finally as a last chance. Non compliance of this direction would lead to dismissal of petition for non prosecution without any further reference. Call on 18.07.2026.

hearings.judge: CCH10 XVIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The counsel for Decree Holder has filed a an application under Order 21 Rule 5 Read with Section 39(4) of CPC., as I.A. No.2 seeking to transfer the decree in O. S. No. 5075/2018 to the Court of the Hon'ble Prl. District and Sessions Judge, Shimogga, for execution of the decree in the interest of justice and equity. Learned Counsel for the JDR submits that he has got no objection to transfer the decree. Heard both side and perused the provisions i.e., Sec.39 of CPC and Rule 106 of the Karnataka Civil Rules of Practice. As can be seen from the cause title of the Award, the J.Dr company is situated at Manjunatha Tower, Near Bharath Gas, Gandhinagar, Shimogga. The counsel for the D.Hr. submits that the Judgment Debtor company is situated within the Jurisdiction of Shimogga District and if the decree is transferred to the above Court, it is easy for the D.Hr. to get the decree executed. This Court is to the considered opinion that, the D.Hr. has made out valid grounds to transfer the decree. Hence, invoking Sec. 39 of CPC., the decree is hereby transferred to the jurisdictional Court/ Hon’ble Prl. District and Sessions Court, Shimogga. On depositing requisite process fee, it is hereby ordered to issue an order in Form No. 3 along with certificate of non-satisfaction of decree in Form No. 4 of Appendix – E of CPC. The office is directed to comply Rule 6 of Order 21 of CPC. File is closed.

hearings.judge: CCH11 VI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case is called out. Cause notice to Decree-holder unserved as not traced. Passed over The Counsel for Decree-holder is present submitted that as per the judgment in WP No.29299/2013 dated 23-10-2024 in case of Mahindra and Mahendra Finance Service Limited v/s K V Chandrashekar and others, the payment of court fee does not arise in respect of award for recovery of money. On perusal of above said judgment. In para 20 observed that award granting recovery of loans advanced does not qualify as an instrument chargeable under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act. In para 21 it observed as follow: An arbitral award should not be subject to any stamp duty under the broad provisions of Section 3(b) when read with Sections 19(a) and (b) due to its unique intangible nature and legislative oversight, which distinguishes an award from other instruments enumerated in the schedule of the Act, which, if executed outside the State of Karnataka and then enforced in the State, would typically incur the stamp duty. And held that stamp duty cannot be subjected to award. The above said judgment is applicable to the case on hand, the facts are similar to that case. Accordingly, office objection is over ruled. Issue cause notice to Judgment Debtors No.1 to 3 through the process of court and by RPAD. Call on: 10-03-2025

hearings.judge: CCH35 XXXIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called out. Counsel for DHR twice called out, absent. On the last date of hearing, this court had directed to the counsel for Dhr to taken steps against Jdr. However, despite the repeated and final opportunities and lapse of considerable time, the decree-holder has failed to appear and prosecute the execution petition diligently. It is relevant to refer to the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs and Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani and Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025, directed all High Courts to ensure that pending execution petitions are disposed of within a period of six months. In view of the long pendency of this execution petition, failure of the decree-holder to take any effective steps and in light of the directions of the Hon’ble Apex Court and the High Court circular, this Court finds no reason to keep this execution petition pending any further. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non-prosecution. The decree-holder is at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law. Office is directed to return the copy of decree to the counsel for DHR upon verification and identification.

hearings.judge: CCH35 XXXIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

Counsel is reminded that, in view of the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs & Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani & Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640–3642/2025, dated 06.03.2025, and Circular No. 2/2025 dated 01.04.2025 issued by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka mandating disposal of execution petitions within six months, this Court is duty bound to prevent unnecessary delay and ensure expeditious disposal of execution petitions.  For steps against Jdr finally as a last chance. Non compliance of this direction would lead to dismissal of petition for non prosecution without any further reference. Call on 18.07.2026.

hearings.business_text: Counsel for Dhr present. Kept by. Again case called out. Counsel for Dhr filed I.A No.2 u/o s 151 of CPC. The said application is accompanied by the affidavit of SPA holder of Dhr. Dhr is entitled to eat fruits of decree. As per nazar report the Jdr has interfered while executing delivery warrant as per order of this Court. Under these facts and circumstances, it is necessary to allow I.A No.2 to meet the ends of justice and equity. Accordingly, I.A No.2 filed u/s 151 of CPC is allowed. hearings.judge: CCH16 XVII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The learned counsel for Dhr has filed I.A No.1 u/o 21 R 35 r/w Sec. 151 of CPC issue delivery warrant against the Jdr to handover vacant possession of suit schedule property. The said application is accompanied by the affidavit of Dhr. Perused materials available on records. This petition is preferred in pursuance of Judgment and Decree passed in O.S No.2627/2017. Appeal was preferred before Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru bearing RFA No.928/2024 which came to be dismissed on 25-09-2024. As per office note also, there is no entry regarding stay or appeal. Heard arguments of counsel for Dhr. The Dhr is entitled to eat fruits of decree. Suit came to be decreed and the defendant was directed to vacate suit schedule property within 3 months from the date of decree. In the present petition legal heirs of Jdr remained absent. Since from 25-09-2024, Jdrs have not vacated the suit schedule property. As stated supra the Dhr is entitled to eat fruits of decreed. Accordingly, to meet the ends of justice and equity, for effective adjudication of petition I.A No.1 filed u/o 21 R 35 r/w Sec. 151 of CPC dated 11-11-2024 is allowed. Issue deliver warrant against Jdrs to handover the vacant possession of the petition schedule property to the Dhr if PF is paid. Call on 09-12-2024.

hearings.business_text: EX 756/2024 Advocate for Decree Holder has filed I.A - under Order 21 Rule 8 r/w Section 39 of CPC , to transfer the decree to Civil Judge & JMFC, Nagamangala. The Decree Holder stated that the Judgment Debtor is residing in the jurisdiction of the Civil Judge & JMFC, Nagamangala, having both movable and immovable property, therefore it is convenient for the Decree Holder to effectively execute the decree. Section 39 of CPC empowers the Court to transfer the Decree either on its own motion or an application filed by the Decree Holder. Perused the documents filed in the execution petition, since the Judgment Debtor is residing in Nagamangala, it is better to transfer the decree to Civil Judge & JMFC, Nagamangala. The parties shall not wait for notice by the Civil Judge & JMFC, Nagamangala and appear before that court on 05.02.2025. hearings.business_text: Case has been called out. Decree holder is present. Counsel for decree holder filed memo. The counsel for Judgment debtor filed objections to I.A. No.1. Case will be taken at post lunch. Case is taken at post lunch. Decree holder and his counsel present. The Judgment debtor and counsel absent. The counsel for the Decree holder addressed the arguments on I.A. No.1. As there is no representation on behalf of Judgment debtor, therefore arguments on I.A. No.1 is taken as not canvassed. Having heard the arguments through the counsel for the Decree holder, I have perused the records. The I.A. No.1 is find U/sec. 151 of Civil Procedure Code on 16.12.2024 by the Decree holder requesting to appoint court Commissioner to break open the lock of the premises to get the physical possession of schedule property. The Judgment debtor in his objections has contended that he has handed over the keys of the premises on 20.01.2024 to the Decree holder. But to substantiate the said fact nothing has been produced. Therefore, it appears that the Judgment debtor still has not deliver the possession of the schedule property. It is evident from the records that the Decree has been passed in favour of the Decree holder directing the Judgment debtor to deliver the vacant physical possession along with arrears of rent and damages along with interest. There is nothing on record to believe that the said Judgment has been either challenged or reversed. Hence, it is just and necessary to appoint the court commissioner to execute the Decree. So, to meet the ends of justice, I proceed to pass the following ORDER I.A. No.1 dated 16.12.2024 filed the Decree holder U/sec 151 of Civil Procedure Code is allowed. Hence, court commissioner Mr. Prakash Hande who is an Advocate has been appointed to carry out commissioner work. The Decree holder is permitted to pay commissioner fee of Rs.5,000/- to the commissioner directly. The court commissioner is directed to deliver the physical possession of the suit schedule property to the Decree holder after breaking open the lock of the premises. Further it is made clear that the concerned jurisdictional police Rajarajeshwari nagar, shall co-operate to the court commissioner in executing the commissioner work. In view of the above, commissioner warrant is issued and also necessary intimation to the jurisdictional police. For report of the commissioner. Call on 24.01.2025.

hearings.judge: CCH38 XXXVII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: This is an execution petition filed for execution of order passed in Misc.No.342/2007, wherein it is ordered that the DHR is entitled to recover a sum of Rs.1,08,45,369/- with interest at the rate of 18% p.a. compounded quarterly rests from the date of the petition till realization. Along with this execution petition IA.No.1/2024 has been filed to transfer the decree to District Judge, Thiruvallur District. The office has raised objections on limitation point. Heard the learned counsel for DHR on the question of Limitation. The order in execution in this petition has been passed in Misc.No.342/2007 on 31.01.2012. The certificate of recovery of amount has been issued. But, the date of issuance of certificate of recovery of amount cannot be made-out. Therefore, the records in Misc.No.342/2007 called for. It shows that the certificate notified on 08.02.2012 and it was signed on 10.02.2012. The present petition has been filed on 30.05.2024, which is after 12 years 3 months. To file an execution petition, the limitation period is 12 years as per Article 136 of Limitation Act 1963. Therefore, the present execution petition filed by the DHR is barred by time. Hence, this execution petition is not maintainable. Accordingly, it is dismissed.

hearings.business_text: JDR advocate filed objection to IA.No. II along with documents. The DHR advocate filed memo along with documents. Jdr advocate filed affidavit of Jdr stating that he should not sell the immovable of property mentioned in the schedule of the petition. But the DHR advocate furnished copy of the sale deed executed by Jdr in favour of K.R. Jayanth dated 14.02.2025 discloses that he already soled the schedule property. Therefore this court opinion that the conduct of the Jdr discloses that he is not come to the court with clean hands and given false information. It is sufficient come to the conclusion that the Jdr may dispose the property in which the DHR seeking attachment. The apprehension in the mind of the DHR should be protected by this court by issuing attachment warrant. Hence issue attachment warrant against the property mentioned in the schedule on I.A.No.II with a direction to the bailiff affix the attachment order in the conspicuous place of schedule property if PF paid. R/by 04.06.2025.

But the DHR advocate furnished copy of the sale deed executed by Jdr in favour of K.R. Jayanth dated 14.02.2025 furnished in the Ex.P.972/2024 discloses that he already soled the schedule property. Therefore this court opinion that the conduct of the Jdr discloses that he is not come to the court with clean hands and given false information. hearings.judge: CCH12 XVI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called. Counsel for DHR present and files memo with details of jurisdictional police. ORDER ON IA DATED 03-08-2024. This I.A. is filed by the DHR U/S 151 of CPC seeking assisstance of jurisdictional police to the Bailiff to break open the lock for attaching movable properties of JDR. In accompanying affidavit to the I.A. it is stated by DHR that the JDR and his nieghbours and his family members did not allow them to their house by not opening the door for attaching movables of JDR intentionally and further they are making threats and creating fear and obstruct for execution of attachment of immovable property. On perusal of counter copy of previous warrant of attachment of movables the bailiff requested for police aid as the father of JDR obstructed him. The learned Counsel for DHR files a memo with details of jurisdictional police as the Jagajeevanramnagar Police Station. If this application is allowed will not cause hardship to other side as the police shall aid to break open with peacefull manner without disturbing anybody in the location of JDR. Hence, this Court proceed to pass the following ORDER I.A. filed by the DHR U/S 151 of CPC for assisstance of jurisdictional police is hereby allowed. Consequently, the concerned police officer of Jagajeevanramnagar Police Station is hereby directed to give aid to the bailiff to break open the lock for attaching movable properties of JDR in the address mentioned in this petition in peacefull manner without disturbing the public. Re-issue attachment warrant of movables with police help.

hearings.judge: CCH67 LXVI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Counsel for decree holder has filed I.A.No.1 under section 151 of CPC r/w Rule 106(4) of Karnataka Civil Rules of Practice to transfer the decree to the Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Maddur and hand over the decree transfer petition to the decree holder. In support of his application DHR has sworn to an affidavit wherein it is stated that Judgment Debtor is residing outside the territorial jurisdiction of this court and transmitting the decree transfer petition through court from this court to jurisdictional court of Maddur will take considerable time and even he may not able to know about exact date of transmission of such orders. Therefore prayed to transfer the decree to the Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Maddur by handing over the decree transfer petition to the hands of the decree holder. The decree holder has assigned a reason that Judgment Debtor is residing outside the jurisdiction of this court and it is stated that he is residing in the jurisdiction of Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Maddur. Hence there is no impediment to transfer the decree to the Principal Civil Judge & JMFC, Maddur. The DHR has sought to handover the decree transfer petition to him for presentation before Principal Civil Judge & JMFC, Maddur. Since the DHR himself has sought for handing over the decree it is just and proper to handover the decree to the DHR for presentation before proper court. Hence the following: ORDER The application filed by the DHR under section 151 CPC r/w Rule 106(4) of Karnataka Civil Rules of Practice is hereby allowed. The decree is ordered to be transferred to the Principal Civil Judge & JMFC, Maddur. A copy of the order transferring the decree together with the accompaniments mentioned in Rule 6 of Order XXI of the Code to be taken to the court to which they are to be sent are ordered to be handed over to the counsel for decree holder on obtaining due acknowledgment.

hearings.business_text: Counsel for DHR has filed I.A. No. 1/2026 under Section 39 r/w Section 151 of CPC to transfer the Execution Petition to Civil Judge and JMFC at K.R. puram. Bengaluru. It is stated in the accompanying affidavit that the JDR is residing out of the jurisdiction of this Court and hence sought to allow the application. Section 39 of CPC provides for transfer of decree to another Court for its execution. In view of the grounds urged and in order to enable the DHR to obtain the fruits of the decree, the IA is allowed. Decree is transferred to the Civil Judge and JMFC at K.R. puram. Bengaluru. Office is directed to comply the provisions of Order 21 Rule 6 of CPC. The present E.P. does not survive for consideration and the E.P. is closed.

hearings.business_text: No representation Matter called twice at 11.30 am and 3.50 pm Orders on IA dated 10.06.2024 On 10.06.2024 the Counsel for DHR has filed IA under Section 39 r/w Section 151 of CPC to transfer the above Petition to Prl. Civil Judge, Bengaluru Rural Court, Bengaluru as the JDR is residing beyond the jurisdiction of this Court. Section 39 of CPC provides for transfer of decree to another court for its execution and it does not contemplate transfer of execution Petition. Therefore the relief sought in the application for transfer of execution Petition is not maintainable. Besides it is noted that the address provided in the cause title of the Petition and the address provided in judgment dated 06.12.2023 of the Judgment Debtor are one and same, no material document is produced before this Court to establish that the JDR is residing beyond jurisdiction of the Court and he is residing within the jurisdiction of Prl. Civil Judge, Bengaluru Rural Court, Bengaluru Hence in absence of material documents no grounds are made to entertain the application, the application is devoid of merits and liable to be rejected. Accordingly IA is rejected with a liberty to file fresh application Call on 07.08.2025

hearings.judge: CCH59 LVIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The present petition arises out of the decree passed on a compromise petition filed by the parties in O.S.No.370/2021 on 22.04.2022. 2. The parties had agreed that the amount of Rs.4,20,000/- shall be waived off from Rs.16,20,000/- that was due. The amount payable would be Rs.12,00,000/-. Thereafter, the defendant/ lessee shall pay Rs.45,000/- continuously without any enhancement as monthly rent to the owner/ lessor. The amount of rent had fallen due since May, 2022. 3. The compromise petition was accompanied by a schedule for payment of the amount that fell due. The decree holder and the judgment debtor have filed the memo of calculation independently. According to the decree holder, the actual amount received from the judgment debtor is Rs.15,15,000/-. Whereas according to the judgment debtor payment made by him until now is Rs.16,00,000/-. The amount that is said to have been paid for which documents are placed on record by the judgment debtor is Rs.7,04,900/- and Rs.1,00,000/- payment made to Smt.Shwetha Maruthi. It is not clear as to who this Smt.Shwetha is which is not specified by the judgment debtor. The judgment debtor is found due in Rs.11,25,000/- towards arrears of rent till the filing of the petition. Even assuming the payment of Rs.15,15,000/-, the judgment debtor would be due in a sum of Rs.23,25,000/-. The judgment debtor would be due in a sum of Rs.8,10,000/-. 4. Now, the learned counsel for the judgment debtor asserts that, in respect of the amount due towards arrears of rent, the decree holder is required to file a separate claim. This apparently is an absurd submission considering the basis on which the compromise petition came to be filed. The decree holder had waived off Rs.4,20,000/- from the amount due and now the judgment debtor submits that, the decree holder has to come up with a fresh petition to recover the amount due under the compromise petition. 5. Considering the conduct of the judgment debtor, I am not inclined to hold that, the decree holder has to file a fresh petition. The judgment debtor in fact has to pay the amount due to the decree holder in order to claim full satisfaction. Office is therefore directed to issue arrest notice to the judgment debtor for payment of the amount due of Rs.13,50,000/-. Call on 21.07.2025.

hearings.judge: CCH35 XXXIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called out. Counsel for DHR twice called out, absent. On the last date of hearing, this court had directed to the counsel for Dhr to taken steps against Jdr. However, despite the repeated and final opportunities and lapse of considerable time, the decree-holder has failed to appear and prosecute the execution petition diligently. It is relevant to refer to the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs and Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani and Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025, directed all High Courts to ensure that pending execution petitions are disposed of within a period of six months. In view of the long pendency of this execution petition, failure of the decree-holder to take any effective steps and in light of the directions of the Hon’ble Apex Court and the High Court circular, this Court finds no reason to keep this execution petition pending any further. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non-prosecution. The decree-holder is at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law. Office is directed to return the copy of decree to the counsel for DHR upon verification and identification.

hearings.business_text: Case called. JDR No.2 and her counsel absent, No representation. Advocate for DHR present. Heard. Perused. On 18.07.2025 advocate for DHR filed a memo stating that, EP may be closed as fully satisfied. The decree is for eviction, directing the defendants to vacate the suit schedule premises after receipt of refundable deposit of Rs.7 lakhs. In this EP this court issued possession delivery warrant which came to be executed as per order sheet dt.06.08.2024. Advocate for DHR filed a memo along with bank statement to show that, as per the decree refundable deposit of Rs.7 lakhs is already paid to the defendants and defendants have handed over the possession of the suit schedule property. The objection of JDR No.2 is that, the DHR has not paid the 50% amount of Rs.7 lakhs to this JDR No.2 as ordered in the decree. On perusal of decree there is no specific order regarding payment of 50% of the refundable deposit to JDR No.2. The order is to repay the refundable deposit of Rs.7 lakhs to the defendants/ JDRs. As per the bank statement the said of amount of Rs.7 lakhs repaid to the defendant No.1 / JDR No.1. JDR No.2 is wife of JDR No.1. Under these circumstance JDR No.2 can recover the amount of her share from JDR No.1. With these observations EP is closed as fully satisfied.

hearings.business_text: Counsel for Decree Holder is present. As per the order of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka dated 23.10.2024 in W.P. 29299/2013 (GM – RES) specifically held that “20) However in the light of the ratios summarized above the instant arbitral award granting recovery of the loans advanced does not qualify as an instrument chargeable under article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. 21) An arbitral award should not be subject to any stamp duty under the broad provisions of Sec.3(b) when read with Sec.19(a) and (b) due to its unique intangible nature and legislative oversight, which distinguishes an award from other instruments enumerated in the schedule of this Act, which, if executed outside the State of Karnataka then enforced in the State would typically incur the stamp duty.” As per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka the compliance of office objection is over ruled. hearings.business_text: Case is called out. Decree-holder absent. Learned Counsel for Decree-holder absent. No representation is made. Again case called at 05.10 PM. Decree-holder absent. Learned Counsel for Decree-holder absent. No representation is made. In this case Decree-holder has not taken steps from 03-03-2025. This court has granted time to the Decree-holder to take steps on 15-04-2025, 04-07-2025, 06-08-2025, 18-09-2025, 27-10-2025, 03-12-2025, 30-01-2026 and 04-03-2026. Hon’ble Supreme Court in Periyammal (dead) through LRs. & ors. v. V. Rajamani & anr. Etc., 2025 INSC 329, has reiterated the guidelines issued in Rahul S. Shah v. Jinendra Kumar Gandhi, (2021) 6 SCC 418 has held as under: 42.12. The executing court must dispose of the execution proceedings within six months from the date of filing, which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay. 42.13. The executing court may on satisfaction of the fact that it is not possible to execute the decree without police assistance, direct the police station concerned to provide police assistance to such officials who are working towards execution of the decree. Further, in case an offence against the public servant while discharging his duties is brought to the knowledge of the court, the same must be dealt with stringently in accordance withlaw. 42.14. The Judicial Academies must prepare manuals and ensure continuous training through appropriate mediums to the court personnel/staff executing the warrants, carrying out attachment and sale and any other official duties for executing orders issued by the executing courts.” The mandatory direction contained in Para 42.12 of Rahul S. Shah (supra) requiring the execution proceedings to be completed within six months from the date of filing, has been reiterated by this Court in its order in Bhoj Raj Garg v. Goyal Education and Welfare Society & ors., Special Leave Petition (C) No. 19654 of 2022. But inspite of granting sufficient time, Decree-holder has not taken steps for execution of decree since last one year. Hence, execution petition is closed for not taking steps.

hearings.business_text: Case is called out. Passed over. Again case called at 03.30 PM. Counsel for Decree-holder files memo with copy of the order in WP No.29299/2013 dated 23-10-2024, in Mahendra and Mahindra Financial Services Limited v/s K V Chandrashekar and another passed by Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka holding that the payment of stamp duty under Article 11 of Karnataka Stamp Act is applicable in respect of award pertain to immovable property, in para 21 of the judgment observed as follows: “21. An arbitral award should not be subject to any stamp duty under the broad provisions of Section 3(b) when read with Sections 19(a) and (b) due to its unique intangible nature and legislative oversight, which distinguishes an award from other instruments enumerated in the Schedule of the Act, which, if executed outside the State of Karnataka and then enforced in the State, would typically incur the stamp duty”. In view of observation by Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka, the award in the present case is in respect of recovery of money as such the question of payment of stamp duty does not arise. Accordingly, office objection is over ruled. Issue cause notice to Judgment Debtors No.1 and 2 through the process of court and by RPAD. Call on: 03-03-2025

hearings.business_text: Case is called out. Passed over. Again case called at 03.30 PM. Counsel for Decree-holder files memo mentioning WP No.29299/2013 dated 23-10-2024, in Mahendra and Mahindra Financial Services Limited v/s K V Chandrashekar and another passed by Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka holding that the payment of stamp duty under Article 11 of Karnataka Stamp Act is applicable in respect of award pertain to immovable property, in para 21 of the judgment observed as follows: “21. An arbitral award should not be subject to any stamp duty under the broad provisions of Section 3(b) when read with Sections 19(a) and (b) due to its unique intangible nature and legislative oversight, which distinguishes an award from other instruments enumerated in the Schedule of the Act, which, if executed outside the State of Karnataka and then enforced in the State, would typically incur the stamp duty”. In view of observation by Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka, the award in the present case is in respect of recovery of money as such the question of payment of stamp duty does not arise. Accordingly, office objection is over ruled. Issue cause notice to Judgment Debtors No.1 and 2 through the process of court and by RPAD. Call on: 03-03-2025

hearings.business_text: Case is called out. Decree-holder absent. Learned Counsel for Decree-holder absent. No representation is made. Again case called at 05.10 PM. Decree-holder absent. Learned Counsel for Decree-holder absent. No representation is made. In this case Decree-holder has not taken steps from 03-03-2025. This court has granted time to the Decree-holder to take steps on 15-04-2025, 04-07-2025, 06-08-2025, 18-09-2025, 27-10-2025, 03-12-2025, 30-01-2026 and 04-03-2026. Hon’ble Supreme Court in Periyammal (dead) through LRs. & ors. v. V. Rajamani & anr. Etc., 2025 INSC 329, has reiterated the guidelines issued in Rahul S. Shah v. Jinendra Kumar Gandhi, (2021) 6 SCC 418 has held as under: 42.12. The executing court must dispose of the execution proceedings within six months from the date of filing, which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay. 42.13. The executing court may on satisfaction of the fact that it is not possible to execute the decree without police assistance, direct the police station concerned to provide police assistance to such officials who are working towards execution of the decree. Further, in case an offence against the public servant while discharging his duties is brought to the knowledge of the court, the same must be dealt with stringently in accordance withlaw. 42.14. The Judicial Academies must prepare manuals and ensure continuous training through appropriate mediums to the court personnel/staff executing the warrants, carrying out attachment and sale and any other official duties for executing orders issued by the executing courts.” The mandatory direction contained in Para 42.12 of Rahul S. Shah (supra) requiring the execution proceedings to be completed within six months from the date of filing, has been reiterated by this Court in its order in Bhoj Raj Garg v. Goyal Education and Welfare Society & ors., Special Leave Petition (C) No. 19654 of 2022. But inspite of granting sufficient time, Decree-holder has not taken steps for execution of decree since last one year. Hence, execution petition is closed for not taking steps.

hearings.business_text: Counsel for the DHR present and files IA No. 2 U/Sec. 151 of CPC and submits that E-khatha is mandatory to register the Court Sale Deed and therefore, prays to direct the jurisdictional BBMP Revenue office to create and register E – Khatha in the name of Registrar, City Civil Court, Bengaluru to facilitate execution of Sale Deed in favour of DHR. In the affidavit supported by the application, the DHR submits that he has filed suit for specific performance against JDR and the same was decreed in his favour. Thereafter, he has filed the present petition seeking execution of the Sale Deed in his favour and also furnished draft copy of the Sale Deed with the office of the Court. It is submitted that the concerned sub-registrar has instructed to obtain E-khatha, which is mandatory as per the applicalbe law, to execute / register Court Sale Deed in favour of DHR. On perusal of the submissions, this Court is of the view that, obtaining E-khatha in favour of City Civil Court, Bengaluru is necessary in order to register Court Sale Deed in favour of DHR. Hence, the IA No.2 is hereby allowed. Consequently, the concerned BBMP revenue officers is hereby directed to create and register the E-khatha in the name of Registrar, City Civil Court, Bengaluru to facilitate execution of the Sale Deed in favour of DHR. The office is hereby directed to send the letter to the concerned BBMP authority for creation and registering the E-khatha in the name of Registrar, City Civil Court, Bengaluru in respect of execution petition schedule property. hearings.business_text: Decree-Holder has sought for attachment of salary of Judgment-Debtor No.2 and 3. As per section.60 of C.P.C. Rs.1000/- and 2 /3rd of the remained cannot be attached in execution of the decree other than decree for maintenance. As per salary slip produce Judgment-Debtor No.2 is drawing net salary of Rs.24,291,/-, Judgment-Debtor No.3 is drawing net salary of Rs.17,254/-, As per execution petition an amount of Rs.97,193/- is due. As per sec.60 an amount of Rs.7,000/- from the salary of Judgment-Debtor No.2, an amount of Rs.4,000/- from the salary of Judgment-Debtor No.3 can be attached. The amount claimed is Rs.97,193/-. Hence, the above mentioned amount can be ordered to be attached for a period of 11 months from the salary of Judgment-Debtor No.2 and 3. Accordingly the salary of Judgment-Debtor No.2 and 3 is attached as mentioned above for a period of 11 months. Office is directed to issue intimation to the drawing officer to deduct the amount of Rs.7,000/- from the salary of Judgment-Debtor No.2, an amount of Rs.4,000/- from the salary of Judgment-Debtor No.3, for a period of 11 months and deposit the same in the court, by 07.01.2025.

hearings.judge: CCH30 XXIX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: ORDERS ON MAINTAINABILITY The D.H.R has filed the present petition to execute the decree passed in O.S. No.6845/2009. The said suit was decreed on 13.04.2010. The present petition was filed on 25.06.2024. It shows that the present petition is filed after lapse of 14 years 2 months and 12 days. As per Article 136 of Limitation Act, the execution petition has to be filed within 12 years from the date of decree enforceable. As per the judgment and decree passed in O.S. No. 3279/2009, the decree can be enforceable from 12.07.2010. But the D.H.R has not filed the present petition within the period of limitation, therefore the decree passed in O.S. No.6845/2009 cannot be executed. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed as barred by limitation.

hearings.judge: CCH31 XXX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: ORDER ON IA NO 2 Counsel for the DHR has filed IA NO 2 U/o 21 R 38 R/w Sec 151 of CPC and prays to pass an order of arrest and detention of the JDR to Civil prison as she likely to abscond. In the affidavit supported by the application, the DHR submitted that, she has filed the present execution petition to recover Rs. 2,04,600/- from the JDR. It is submitted that the matter settled between the DHR and JDR before the Lok Adalath. However, the JDR is avoiding to make payment, hence, prays to allow the application. In this regard it is relevant to refer Sec. 56 of CPC which reads as follows:- “Sec. 56 :- Prohibition of Arrest or detention of women in execution of Decree for money. - Not withstanding anything in this part, the Court shall not order the arrest or detention in the Civil prison of a women in execution of a decree for the payment of money”. Therefore, the law clearly bars the arrest of women in an execution proceedings for payment of money. Hence, the application deserves to be rejected. ORDER The IA No 2 filed by the DHR U/o 21 R 38 R/w Sec. 151 of CPC is hereby rejected. Further, the DHR is at liberty to take alternative step against the JDR for recovery of money in accordance with law. For further steps by 24/4/26.

hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: DHR files memo stating that, this court was pleased to decree their suit on 24.04.2009, the JDR herein preferred an appeal in RFA 28/10, which came to be dismissed on 22.01.2013, but this Ex.petition being filed on 09.07.2024. thus the contention of the DHR is that, though decree being granted on 24.04.2009, if the period spent before the appeal, that is upto 22.01.2013 is requires to be excluded for computing limitation for filing the Ex.petition. If that aspect is considered, from the date of dismissal of RFA, the DHR filed the Ex.Petition within 12 yrs, thus same is well in time. Upon hearing the arguments and perusal of the provision u/sec 15(1) of Limitation Act found that, the period spent before the Appellant court will be excluded only if there was an injunction from institution and execution of decree, but in RFA 28/10, the appellant fails to comply the office objection for a period of 3 yrs, thus same got dismissed for default, it means to say in the appeal no stay of institution or execution of the decree being granted. If that aspect is considered, mere filing of appeal is not sufficient to exclude the period on which the appeal was pending, thus the contention of the DHR cannot be accepted. As the Ex.Petition being filed more than after 14 yrs from the date of decree, thus the Ex.Petition is filed after expiry of the limitation of 12 yrs, thus the petition of the DHR is hereby dismissed as it is barred by time.
