hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: DHR files memo stating that, this court was pleased to decree their suit on 24.04.2009, the JDR herein preferred an appeal in RFA 28/10, which came to be dismissed on 22.01.2013, but this Ex.petition being filed on 09.07.2024. thus the contention of the DHR is that, though decree being granted on 24.04.2009, if the period spent before the appeal, that is upto 22.01.2013 is requires to be excluded for computing limitation for filing the Ex.petition. If that aspect is considered, from the date of dismissal of RFA, the DHR filed the Ex.Petition within 12 yrs, thus same is well in time. Upon hearing the arguments and perusal of the provision u/sec 15(1) of Limitation Act found that, the period spent before the Appellant court will be excluded only if there was an injunction from institution and execution of decree, but in RFA 28/10, the appellant fails to comply the office objection for a period of 3 yrs, thus same got dismissed for default, it means to say in the appeal no stay of institution or execution of the decree being granted. If that aspect is considered, mere filing of appeal is not sufficient to exclude the period on which the appeal was pending, thus the contention of the DHR cannot be accepted. As the Ex.Petition being filed more than after 14 yrs from the date of decree, thus the Ex.Petition is filed after expiry of the limitation of 12 yrs, thus the petition of the DHR is hereby dismissed as it is barred by time.

hearings.business_text: Case called out. Counsel for DHR twice called out, absent. On the last date of hearing, this court had directed to the counsel for Dhr to take further steps against Jdr. However, despite the repeated and final opportunities and lapse of considerable time, the decree-holder has failed to appear and prosecute the execution petition diligently. It is relevant to refer to the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs and Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani and Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025, directed all High Courts to ensure that pending execution petitions are disposed of within a period of six months. In view of the long pendency of this execution petition, failure of the decree-holder to take any effective steps and in light of the directions of the Hon’ble Apex Court and the High Court circular, this Court finds no reason to keep this execution petition pending any further. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non-prosecution. The decree-holder is at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law. Office is directed to return the copy of decree to the counsel for DHR upon verification and identification.

hearings.judge: CCH42 XLI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: On 18.07.2024 Counsel for DHR has filed IA under Section 39 r/w Order 21 Rule 6 of CPC requesting the Court to direct the office to issue decree transfer certificate to Prl. Senior Civil Judge, Shivajinagar, Pune. It is averred in the affidavit sworn by DHR that movable and immovable properties of JDR are situated out side the jurisdiction of this Court and hence it is necessary to transfer the decree for execution to the Court at Pune. It is further submitted that transfer of decree would enable him to effectively to secure fruits of decree and thus sought to allow the application. Heard the DHR. Upon perusal of the grounds urged in the application and the cause title of the judgment in OS No. 3698/2023 it is evident that the defendant is a proprietorship concern having its business at Pune. Hence this Court is of the opinion that the DHR has satisfied this Court that the JDR is carrying on his business at Pune and the JDR is not having any properties within the jurisdiction of this Court to satisfied the decree. Hence in order to enable the DHR to obtain the fruits of the decree, the IA is allowed. Decree is transferred to the Court of Prl. Senior Civil Judge, Shivajinagar, Pune. Office is directed to comply the provisions of Order 21 Rule 6 of CPC. The present E.P. does not survive for consideration and the E.P. is closed.

hearings.business_text: Counsel for DHr filed IA.No.4/2024 u/O 6 R 17 of CPC. Heard the learned counsel for DHr. Perused the records. This is an execution petition filed by the DHr to execute the decree passed in OS.No.154/201 dated 12.03.2024. The said suit has been decreed by granting the reliefs of declaration of title, possession and permanent injunction with costs. DHr has already taken possession of the property. Now the petition is pending for recovery of cost in the decree, total costs is stated as Rs.2,96,280/-. The DHr counsel submitted that due to oversight and typographical error in the execution petition total costs is mentioned as Rs.11,928/-, but it ought to have been Rs.2,96,280/-. It appears that mistake crept in preparing the execution petition. It is a typographical error. Hence, DHr has made out grounds for allowing the application. Accordingly, IA.No.4/2024 is allowed. No cost. DHr is permitted to carryout the amendment in the petition and to furnish amended petition. Same by 11-11-2024

hearings.business_text: EX 1604/2024 Learned counsel for DHR and JDR present. Heard the argument of Learned counsel for DHR and JDR No.5 and 6. For orders. ORDER The present DHRs had filed O.S.No.2488/2012 seeking partition and separate possession, the same was decreed. In the said judgment and decree of the O.S.No.2488/2012 Defendant No.4 by name M.N.Chandrashekar who is JDR No.5 herein was directed to pay the maintenance of Rs.20,000/- to the Plaintiff’s who are DHRs herein, out of the income derived from the properties mentioned in the decree, untill the payment of 1/4th share of the Plaintiff’s in the sale consideration amount of item No.1 to 5 in “C” schedule properties. As being the fact in view of the judgment and decree passed by this court the present DHRs who are Plaintiff’s in the aforesaid suit have filed EP, seeking the maintenance from JDR No.5. On the other hand the JDR No.5 by name M.N.Chandrashekar and JDR No.6 M.N.Yaswanthkumar who were Defendant No.4 and 5 in O.S.2488/2012 have objected for the Petition and further JDR No.5 and 6 contended that 2 appeals in namely RFA No.635/2024 and RFA 588/2024 are filed before Hon'ble High court of Karnataka, but there is no stay of this present proceedings by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka. Further JDR No.5 and 6 have not made out any grounds to reject the present petition. Hence under these circumstances the JDR No.5 by name M.Nchandrashekar, who is Defendant No.4 in O.S.No.2488/2012 shall comply the order of the court to pay the maintenance amount to the DHRs, untill payment of 1/4th share of the Plaintiff’s in the sale consideration amount of item No.1 to 5 of “C” schedule properties. Hence the DHRs are at liberty to take steps for realization of the maintenance amount as per the judgment and decree passed in the aforesaid suit. In view of the aforesaid reasons this court feels it just and proper to issue attachment warrant of movables of JDR No.5 who is Defendant No.4 in O.S.No.2488/2012 if PF paid. Call on 24.07.2025.

hearings.judge: CCH32 XX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called out. Perused the petition and the records and I.A No.I/24. After perusal of the records, it is found that J.Drs neither residing nor running their business within the jurisdiction of this court. The records further reveals that J.Drs are also not having any movable or immovable property/ies within the jurisdiction of this court. When J.Drs are not residing or not running their business or not working for gain within jurisdiction of this court and when they are also not having any kind of property within the jurisdiction of this court, the execution of the decree by this court is not possible. Hence, the decree requires to be transferred to the court in whose jurisdiction the J.Drs are actually residing or running their business or working for gain. Therefore, I proceed to pass the following ORDER Office is hereby directed to transfer the decree, a certificate (as stated in Rule 6 of Order XXI CPC) and related records to the jurisdictional court i.e Hon\''ble Principal Districtl Judge at Puduchery for execution of decree, if PF is paid. And further directed to put up the file after receipt of the report from the executing court.

hearings.judge: CCH61 LX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Counsel for the decree holder has filed the advancement application therefore case is taken on board. Decree holder is present. The counsel for the decree holder has filed IA No.1 under Order 21 Rule 35 of Civil Procedure Code requesting to issue delivery warrant and also submitted process memo. Heard and perused. It is seen that, the Judgment debtors are remained absent and not pursuing the matter till today. It means they remained unrepresented. It is further evident that, this court has decreed suit O.S. No. 5589/2022 directing the defendant to hand over the vacant possession of suit schedule property and also directed the defendants to pay arrears of rent. As against, the said judgment and decree the Judgment debtors filed RFA No. 844/2024. But, the Decree holder has filed affidavit submitting that there is no stay in the said regular first appeal and even Judgment debtors are not pursuing the matter and even they have not made compliance till this day. After perusal of the records, it is opined that it is just and necessary to issue delivery warrant as sought for. Hence, to meet the ends of justice I proceed to pass the following: ORDER Delivery warrant is ordered to be issued against the Judgment debtors in respect of schedule property. The bailiff is directed to execute the delivery warrant and submit the report. For report Call on 25.03.2025.

hearings.judge: CCH12 XVI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Counsel for DHR present. Sri.MS advocate present and files vakalath for JDR no.2. Counsel for DHR files I.A no.1 U/S 151 of CPC. Kept by for orders. Order on I.A No.1. I.A No.1 filed U/S 151 of CPC by the DHR seeking order to issue delevery warrant by breaking open of the door of the schedule premises with the help of police protection and to hand over vacant possession of the suit schedul premisess to the DHR in the interest of justice. In their company affidavit to I.A it is stated that while the court ameen along with DHR went to suit schedule premises for taking possession of schedule premises on 28.08.2024 vide order dated 21.09.2024 the JDR have locked the premises and delevery warrant was returned unexecuted. It is further stated that the delevery warrant could not be executed on account of lock of schedule premises by JDRs. As the JDRs are very power full persons and they mey obstruct the execution of delevery warrant and without help of police the delevery warrant cannot be executed for taking possession of schedule premises. Hence, Prays to allow the I.A. On perusal of material on record it found that the belief endorsed in delevery warrant that he needs police protection to open the lock of the door as it required as per situation of the spot. Here in this case though the JDR is present but as per judgment in O.S No.5557/2022 the defence of defendant was strike out as per direction of Hon’ble high court of Karnataka. As per decree in said suit it is ordered by this court by way of direction directing the defendants to quit, vacate and handover vacant, physical possesion of the schedule premisess with keys to the Plaintiffs. And further by way of consequential order of direction directing the defendant to pay the arriers of rent as damages and so also the maintanance charges totally of Rs.6,30,000/- from 03.12.2020 to 03.03.2022 and thereafter till realization with the interest thereon. As on executing court this court cannot go beyond the decree and in the Original suit itself the defence of defendant was strike out hence if this application is allowed will not cause prejudise to the otherside. If the I.A is allowed with direction to jurisdictional police to give aid in execution of issuance of delevery warrant by breaking open the lock of door of schedule premises with peacefull manner will leads to justice. Accordingly this court proceed to pass the following: ORDER The I.A no.1 filed by the DHR U/S 151 of CPC is hereby allowed. Consequently it is hereby directed to the office to issue delevery warrant by breaking open the lock of the door of schedule premises with the help of police protection and to hand over vacan possession of the schedule premises to the DHR. Accordingly the concerned jurisdictional police are hereby directed to give aid and protection to the balief and DHR along with his Counsel while executing this order in the schedule premises with peaceful manner without harming the person and property in the location of suit schedule premises. The Counsel for DHR directed to furnish details of jurisdictional police in the office to comply this order. Office is hereby directed to re-issue delevery warrant as per this order. Call on 05.11.2024

hearings.judge: CCH17 II ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The case is again called at 3.15 P.M. DHR called out absent. No representation. On perusal of records, this execution petition filed to enforce the award passed in LAC 332/2001 dated 24-11-2009. The DHR along with execution petition also filed IA No.1 U/sec 5 of the Limitation Act praying to condone the delay of 300 days in filing the this execution petition. Any decree or award can be enforced within twelve years from the date of award / Decree. Undisguisedly the award in LAC 332/2001 passed as on 24-11-2009, as such the DHR ought to have filed this execution petition on or before 24-11-2021. This execution petition filed as on 11-09-2024. As such there was a delay of 2 years 3 months and not 300 days. The said delay was not at all explained in the affidavit filed in support of IA No.1 wherein it is simply stated that DHR was not feeling well, but not explained since from what date till what date, the DHR was not keeping well. Under such circumstances, certainly this execution petition is not maintainable as the execution petition is barred by limitation. Apart from that no representation on behalf of the DHR when ever the case is called out and even the DHR is remained absent. No purpose will be served by keeping the file alive. Hence, the following: ORDER The execution petition is hereby dismissed for default and execution petition is barred by limitation.

hearings.business_text: D.Hr counsel present and files IA No.1 U/S 39 r/w sec. 151 of CPC to transfer the decree to court of Prl. Senior Civil Judge, Bengaluru Rural District. Senior Civil Judge, Bengaluru Rural District stating that the J.Dr has having movable and immovable property and his place of residence is No.52, Immadihalli, Near Post Office, Whitefield, Varthur Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluk, Bengaluru-66 and the said place of residence comes within the jurisdictional of Prl. Senior Civil Judge, Bengaluru Rural District. Hence the D.Hr prays to transfer the execution petition as prayed in the application. Heard, IA No.1 is allowed. Office is directed to transfer the execution petition to the Prl. Senior Civil Judge, Bengaluru Rural District as per law.

hearings.judge: CCH18 XIX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Both counsel present. Counsel for the Decree Holder has stated that Judgment Debtor has neither paid rent amounting to Rs.5,35,000/- to be paid in 3 installments that ended on 31.10.2024 nor he has vacated suit schedule property as per compromise decree entered between them in O.S.No.324/2024. It is further stated that the son of Decree Holder is doing employment is staying in rented house because of non-vacation of the property by Judgment Debtor, who is squatting on the schedule premises without paying any arrears of rent. On the other hand, Judgment Debtor is absent. Counsel for the Judgment Debtor prays time to vacate the suit property. The medical reports furnished by counsel for Judgment Debtor dated 09.10.2024 and that he is suffering from illness. These are not the grounds to squat on petition schedule premises. There is no medical report as on today and also there is no impediment for Judgment Debtor to quit/vacate petition schedule premises. Having given no reasonable grounds or justification for being in the petition schedule premises and in paying arrears of rent, the objection raised by Counsel for the Judgment Debtor cannot be considered. Judgment Debtor has not complied the terms and conditions mentioned compromise decree as he has neither paid arrears of rent nor vacated suit premises which he ought to have vacated at the end of October 2024. No purpose will be served in giving time to Judgment Debtor which ultimately frustrates the decree and which also deprives Decree Holder to enjoy the fruits of the decree. Issue delivery warrant against Judgment Debtor if steps taken. It is to be noted that Decree Holder can proceed against Judgment Debtor in issuance of delivery warrant against Judgment Debtor only after 15 days from today. Call on 03.04.2025.

hearings.business_text: ORDERS ON I.A. NO.4 The present IA. No.4 dtd: 04.03.2025 is filed by the Decree holder No.5 under Order 22 Rule 10 of Civil Procedure Code r/w Section 151 of Civil Procedure Code seeking permission to implead opponents as a Judgment debtors in the present case. In support of application the said Decree holder No.5 has filed affidavit. Counsel for the opponents – objectors has submitted that he has no objections. Heard and perused. It is seen from the affidavit of the Decree holder that during the pendency of the suit the present opponents - objectors has purchased the suit property under sale deed dtd: 09.08.2024, therefore, they are necessary parties to the present execution petition. In support of application the Decree holder has furnished the photocopies of sale deeds. As can be seen from the records, the opponents - objectors filed I.A No.1 for seeking permission to enter into the execution petition on the guise that, they have purchased the suit property. The said application is still pending. Upon considering the facts of the case, it is opined that the present opponents are necessary to the present execution petition for proper adjudication. It is further opined that, if the application is rejected, the same leads to unnecessary multiplication of proceedings. Hence, to meet the ends of justice I proceed to following: ORDER I.A. No.4 dtd: 04.03.2025 filed by the Decree holder No.5 under Order 22 Rule 10 of Civil Procedure Code r/w Section 151 of Civil Procedure Code is allowed. No order as to cost. In view of the above, the Decree holder are permitted to implead the opponents as Judgment debtors. Call on 08.04.2025.

hearings.business_text: Ex 2063/2024 Case called out. Counsel for Dhr filed memo stating that decree has been fully satisfied and Dhr does not want to prosecute the petition and pray to dismiss the petition as fully satisfied. Perused the memo, heard the counsel for D.Hr and passed the following: ORDER The memo filed by the D.Hr is hereby accepted and allowed. Petition is hereby closed as fully satisfied.

hearings.judge: CCH32 XX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Ex No 2063/2024 Case is advanced by the Learned Counsel for D.Hr and hence matter is taken up for today's board. Both learned counsels for the parties present. Received the delivery warrant as the daughter of the J.Dr not open the door of the premise and sought for police help for beak open the premise. Counsel for D.Hr files I.A. no.I/26 U/o 21 rule 24 R/w sec 151 of CPC seeking police assistance for executing the delivery warrant. Counsel for D.Hr submitted that as per the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru in RFA no.472/2018 (EJE) , the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru directed the J.Dr to vacate and hand over the premise on or before 30.09.2024 subject to clear the entire arrears of rent. Counsel for D.Hr further submitted that from the date of filing of the suit till today J.Dr has not paid the rent and also not handed over the premise to D.Hr and now the J.Dr is obstructing to execute the delivery warrant. Counsel for J.Dr submits that D.Hr is not a proper representative and one more connected suit is pending in O.S.No.539/2025 before the CCH-43. However there is no stay with respect to the execution and judgment and decree in this case is attained finality in RFA nso .472/2018 (EJE) Hence this court finds that there is no merit in the submissions made by the J.Dr. Hence I.A. no.I/26 filed by the Counsel for the D.Hr is hereby allowed. Reissue delivery warrant with the police assistance and permission to break open the lock of the premise, if PF paid by 26.02.2026.

hearings.business_text: Learned counsel appearing for D.Hr. has filed a memo stating that the vacant possession of the suit schedule property was handed over to them on 08.11.2024 and sought for to close the execution petition. Hence in view of the memo, the execution petition is closed as fully satisfied.

hearings.judge: CCH15 VIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Learned counsel appearing for D.Hr. has filed I.A.No.1 u/o 21 Rule 22 r/w/s 151 of C.P.C. to dispensed the notice against the J.Dr. and sought for to issue delivery warrant of the petition schedule property. Examined the records. The J.Dr. has preferred RFA No. 2054/2022 before the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka against the Judgment and Decree passed in OS 3061/2019. In the said RFA, the J.Dr. has filed an affidavit undertaking to vacate the suit schedule premises on or before 28.02.2024 and the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA 2054/2022 dated 14.12.2022 has observed that the J.Dr. shall handover the vacant possession of the suit schedule premises on or before 28.02.2024 to the decree holders. Thereafter, the J.Dr. filed an application seeking for extension of period of 6 months to vacate the suit schedule premises from 28.02.2024. The Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka by its order dated 06.03.2024 in RFA 2054/2022 has rejected the application filed by the J.Dr. seeking for extension of period by 6 months to vacate the suit schedule premises. Therefore, it appears that the J.Dr. has failed to vacate the petition schedule premises as undertaken given by him before the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka on or before 28.02.2024. Hence, I.A.No.1 is allowed. Issuance of notice to J.Dr. is dispensed. Issue delivery warrant against J.Dr. to hand over the vacant possession of the petition schedule property to the decree holders if PF paid. R/by 30.11.2024.

hearings.business_text: I.A. No.1 filed by JDR No.2 U/S 151 of CPC seeking to recall the order dated 26-10-2024 and to withdraw the deliverry warrant issued against JDR No.2. In accompanying affidavit to the I.A. it is stated that the DHR supressed the facts and filed this E.P. for illegal and immoral game. This Court passed Judgment on 19-04-2024, however not issued on that date since DHR not paid proper court fees and paid only Rs.31,627/- instead of Rs.71,427/-. Hence, holded the decree. In mean time defendant No.2 / JDR No.2 preferred RFA No.2018/24 but due to non production of decree the Registry has raised office Objections. Subsequently in the month of September 2024 the DHR paid the deficit court fee and thereafter this Court signed the decree on 20-09-2024. Hence, appeal period commence from 90 days from the date of decree. As RFA is pending before Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka by misleading and suppressing the fact filed this petition. If this application is dismissed the JDR No.2 will suffer hardship and mysery as his family and kids residing in Suit Schedule premesis. Hence, prayed to allow the I.A. On the other hand the DHR filed Objections contending that this application is not maintainable as the Judgment and decree is not stayed by the Appellat Court. In the original Suit O.S. No.6877/21 which is filed for releif of eviction and for arrears for rent, damages and for other releifs. As per Judgment dated 09-04-2024 this Court directed to defendant No.2 to hand over vacant possession of Suit Schedule Property and other releif for payment of arrears of rent with interest. It is stated that if this application is allowed than he will suffer grate hardship and loss. Heard, perused materials placed on record. As per the order in O.S.No.6877/2021 this JDR No.2 is directed to vacat, deliver and hand over vacant possession of Suit Schedule Property. But defendant No.1 liable to pay arrears of rent. As per the said document defendant No.1 placed exparte. It shows that the defendant No.2 paying the rent to defendant No.1 as found in said judgment. This Court defenitely can not go beyond the decree. In support of this application the JDR No.2 has not filed any documents and there is no stay from appeallat Court. Therefore JDR No.2 has not made out any ground to allow the I.A. Accordingly this Court proceed to pass the following ORDER I.A. No.1 filed by the JDR No.2 U/S 151 of CPC is hereby rejected. Await delivery warrant. Call on 10-01-2025.

hearings.business_text: Counsel for Dhr filed memo to close the execution petition as fully satisfied stating that Jdrs have handed over the suit schedule property to the Dhr and yet another memo along with the order passed in SLP(Civil) No.45532/2025 stating that the SLP preferred by Jdrs against the Judgment passed in RFA No.1124/2025 clubbed with RFA No.632/2015 has been dismissed on 16-09-2025. hearings.judge: CCH16 XVII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The matter is listed today for orders on I.A No.1 and 2. In the present forenoon session itself, the counsel for Jdr No.2 to 5 filed memo stating that Jdr No.2 to 5 filed appeal before Hon’ble Supreme Court in SLP Diary No.45532/2025 against the Judgment dated 24-09-2024 in RFA No.1124/2015 c/w RFA No.632/2015 and in this connection they filed compluter generated copy of Diary No.45532/2025. By filing memo to the said effect, counsel for Jdr No.2 to 5 prays this court to withhold the orders to be passed on I.A No.1 and 2. But, on perusal of the memo and document attached to the same, it becomes clear that no stay order is currently inforce to come in the way of enforcing the decree passed in O.S No.4968/2006. Added further to this, the court could not ignore that since 2006 the Dhr is before court and even after passing of decree, he is not in a position to reap the fruits of decree. Wherefore, the submission of the counsel for Jdr No.2 to 5 to withhold the orders to be passed on I.A No.1 and 2 is rejected. As a consequence, the court perused I.A No.1 and 2 both filed by Dhr u/s 151 of CPC to issue delivery warrant and to order for police help to execute the delivery warrant with break open the lock and also perused the affidavits filed in support of these 2 applications. The Jdrs filed common objections to I.A No.1 and 2 objecting that Jdr are in exclusive possession and enjoyment of the property and there are permanent structure and several valuable things are there in the premises and in order to shift the same from one place to another it requires time. Further, objects that the Dhr is making several attempts to grab the property of Jdr without due process of law. Therefore, it is prayed to dismiss the application. The court find no substance in the objections as raised by Jdrs. Because if the Dhr is intending to dispose the Jdrs without due process of law, he would never approach this court with O.S No.4968/2006. Apparently, the said suit came to be decreed way back in the year 2015 i.e. on 13-03-2015 and the appeals preferred against the Judgment in RFA No.1124/2015 c/w RFA No.632/2015 came to be dismissed on 24-09-2024. Now the Jdrs raised objections that the require time to shift the movable properties, which is not acceptable. The court is conscientious that this is 19 years old litigation and the Dhr could not enjoy the fruits of the decree even after dismissal of aforesaid appeals. Wherefore, it is obvious to allow I.A No.1 and 2 or otherwise the decree will become a paper decree. Accordingly, the court proceed to pass following: ORDER I.A No.1 and 2 both filed by Dhr u/s 151 of CPC are allowed. Dhr paid process memo. Issue delivery warrant as prayed in I.A No.1 and deliver information to the jurisdictional police i.e. City Market Police Station to assist the court officer to execute the delivery warrant effectively by 20-09-2025.

hearings.business_text: The learned counsel for the DHr files I.A.No.1 U/s 151 of CPC seeking the order of Delivery Warrant with a direction to break-open the lock of the suit schedule property. The said application is supported by the affidavit of the DHr, wherein it is stated that the JDr has locked the door of the suit schedule property and hence the Bailiff has returned the Delivery Warrant issued by this Court for want of order of the breaking open the lock. I have perused the report of the Bailiff. It is forthcoming in the said report that the Execution schedule property is kept under the lock. I have perused the Judgment and Decree passed by this Court in O.S No.7965/2022. In the said Judgment and Decree it was directed to the Defendant to quit and delivery the vacant possession of the suit schedule property within 90 days from the date of the Judgment and Decree dated 22.07.2024. Such 90 days was completed in the month of October, 2024 itself. As the delivery of possession was not completed as per the Judgment and Decree, present Petition is filed. As stated above, the Judgment Debtor has kept the premises of the Execution Petition Schedule under the lock. Hence in my opinion, I.A.No.1 filed by the learned counsel for the DHr need to be allowed for completing the execution process of Delivery Warrant. Hence I proceed to pass the following ORDER I.A.No.1 filed by the learned counsel for the DHr U/s 151 of CPC is hereby allowed. Office is directed to issue Delivery Warrant with a direction to break-open the lock of schedule premises of the Execution Petition, returnable by 25.11.2025.

hearings.judge: CCH40 XXXIX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called out. Learned counsel for DHR present. Learned counsel for DHR filed memo stating that the instant execution petition seeking recovery of the decree amount from the JDR who are residing within the jurisdictional limits ascribed in application i.e., Doddaballapura District. Perused, heard a perusal of materials on records reveals that the Judgment Debtors are residing out side the jurisdictional limits of this court, so as to say with the jurisdictional Limit of IV Addl. District and Sessions Court, Doddaballapura Court. Hence for due and effective execution of decree issuance or order of precepts would enable Decree holder to enure fruits of decree, accordingly office is hereby directed to issue order of precepts before court of IV Addl. District and Sessions Court, Doddaballapura Court by ascertaining the division where it has to be issued under the provisions contemplated under section 46 of Civil Procedure Code. In light of said observation instant execution petition stands disposed thereof with due notice thereupon.

hearings.judge: CCH40 XXXIX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called out. Learned counsel for DHR present and filed IA under Sec.39 of the CPC. Heard counsel for the DHR and perused the records. The DHR intends to transfer the petition to the jurisdictional court. As per Sec.39 of CPC if such person has no property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of the court which pass the decree and has property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of such other court and if the person against whom the decree is passed resides within the local limits of the jurisdiction such other court, then the court which passes the decree may send it for execution to such other court and transfer the decree to such other court. On perusal of the execution petition it reveals that the JDRs are residing at Vapasandra, Chikkaballapura District. Hence, by applying the above provision the decree can be transferred to the court as sought in the application. With this observation, I proceed to pass the following ORDER IA filed by DHR under Sec.39 of CPC is hereby allowed. Office is directed to transfer the decree to the Hon'ble Prl. District and Sessions Judge at Chikkaballapura. Accordingly instant Execution petition is closed and disposed otherwise.

Rajamani and another etc., dated 06.03.2025, it is held that, The executing court must dispose of the execution proceedings within six months from the date of filing, which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay. In view of above said judgment, the decree holder has not taken effective steps. There are no grounds to proceed further. Hence, this petition is closed for time being. Office is hereby directed to return the certified copy of decree / award copy to decree holder on proper identification.

hearings.business_text: Case is called out. The EP is filed for recovery of amount based on award is passed by the sole Aribitrator. Office has made a note stamp duty on award amount has not paid. The Counsel for Decree-holder relied upon judgment in WP No.29299/2013 dated 23-10-2024 in case of Mahindra and Mahendra Finance Service Limited v/s K V Chandrashekar and other. In para 20 of the judgment observed that award granting recovery of loans advanced does not qualify as an instrument chargeable under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act. In para 21 it obsered as follow: An arbitral award should not be subject to any stamp duty under the broad provisions of Section 3(b) when read with Sections 19(a) and (b) due to its unique intangible nature and legislative oversight, which distinguishes an award from other instruments enumerated in the schedule of the Act, which, if executed outside the State of Karnataka and then enforced in the State, would typically incur the stamp duty. And held that stamp duty cannot be subjected to award. The above said judgment is applicable to the case on hand, the facts are similar to that case. Accordingly, office objection is over ruled. Issue cause notice to Judgment Debtors No.1 and 2 through the process of court and by RPAD. Call on: 17-01-2025

hearings.judge: CCH30 XXIX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: On perusal of the records, it discloses that the D.H.R has filed the present petition for execution of the arbitral award passed in AA No.2023/SBI/ARB/075941. The arbitral award passed by Arbitrator at Delhi. To execute the said award, the present petition is being filed. Learned counsel for the D.H.R. has relied upon the decision of Sundram Finance Ltd. Vs Abdul Samad and Anr., wherein the Hon’ble Apex Court has held that the enforcement of an award through its execution can be filed anywhere in the country where such a decree can be executed and there is no requirement for obtaining a transfer of decree from the Court, which would have jurisdiction over the arbitral proceedings. In view of the ration laid down in the above decision, it is very clear that the execution petition can be filed in anywhere of the country to execute the arbitration award. There is no necessity to seek transfer of award u/s 39 of C.P.C. Hence, there is no impediment on this Court to entertain this petition. As the present petition is filed within 2 years from the date of award, the provision under Order 21 Rule 22 of C.P.C. does not envisages to issue cause notice to the J.D.R. hence, It is just and proper to issue attachment warrant for movables against J.D.R. P.F. and list of movables furnished. Hence, office is hereby directed to issue attachment warrant for movables against J.D.R by 21.02.2025.

hearings.business_text: In this case office of this court raised objection stating that stamp duty is not paid and the D.hr advocate furnished copy of order passed by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P.No.29299 of 2013 (GM-RES) dated 23/10/2024. The counsel for D.hr argued that since it is a money decree, the payment of stamp duty is not necessary. In support of his contention he has furnished the copy of order passed by Hon’ble High Court. In the said order the Hon’ble High Court by considering various decisions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court and Hon’ble High Courts and Section 11 of Karnataka Stamp Act held that the instant arbitral award granting recovery of the loans advanced does not qualify as an instrument chargeable under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957. Hence this court find that payment of stamp duty on award in money suit is not necessary. Hence the office objection is overruled. Issue cause notice to J.dr 1 and 2 by 19/4/2025.

hearings.business_text: The learned counsels for the Decree holder and Judgment debtor are present. The learned counsel for the Decree holder filed I.A.No.1 under Order 26 Rule 18A Read with Section 151 of CPC. The learned counsel for the Judgment debtor prayed time to object on I.A.No.1. Heard. This is a decree under execution arisen out of the settlement arrived between the parties before the Mediation and inspite of the settlement arrive between them, the Judgment debtor has not complied with terms and conditions of the memorandum of settlement. The only objection of the learned counsel for the Judgment debtor submitted before the Court is that the Decree holder filed several execution petitions ealier and this is the 4th execution petition. But, it is not the case of Judgment debtor that the Judgment debtor has satisfied the decree. Therefore, the objection of the learned counsel for the Judgment debtor is not sustainable and no time can be granted to Judgment debtor to oppose I.A.No.1. To execute the decree in terms of the Memorandum of settlement, it is just and necessary to appoint the Court Commissioner to execute the rectification deed in terms of the decree. Hence, I.A.No.1 filed by the Decree holder is hereby allowed. Smt. Lavanya K, Advocate is appointed as Court Commissioner to execute the rectification deed on behalf of the Court in favour of the Decree holder. The Commissioner fee is fixed Rs.5000/-. The Decree holder is directed to pay the Commissioner fee directly to the Court Commissioner and report the same to the Court. Issue Commissioner warrant if PF is paid. Call on 05.08.2025.

hearings.judge: CCH25 III ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Counsel for the DHR present. Case again called out at 3.20P.M. Counsel for the DHR present. Heard on I.A.NO. 1. This I.A.NO. 1 is filed u/sec 39 of CPC for transferring the petition to the competent jurisdiction court for the reason assigned in the annexed affidavit. This affidavit sworned by authorized person of DHR company. In para No.4 of annexed affidavit DHR stated that the assestes of JDR against the whom decree is passed are situated in Secandrabad, Hydrabad Dist, Telagana State. Therefore, prays to allow the application by transferring the said petition to the competent jurisdiction court Secandrabad, Hydrabad Dist, Telgana State. As per section 39(c) of CPC “ if such person as no property within the local limits of jurisdiction of the court which passed the decree sufficient to satisfied such decree directs the sale or delivery of immovable property situate outside the local limits of the jurisdiction of the court which passed it”. Here in the case on hand the property of the JDR is situated in outside the jurisdiction of this court. In view of the provision of above the I.A.NO.1 u/sec 39 of CPC by the DHR company is hereby allowed. The execution petition is transferred to district sessions and civil court at Secandrabad, Hydrabad Dist, Telagana State. Office is hereby directed to transfer to entire record to district sessions and civil court at Secandrabad, Hydrabad Dist, Telagana State.

hearings.business_text: Counsel for decree holder is present. In judgment passed by Honble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642 of 2025 in case of Peruyammal (Dead Through Lrs.) Vs V. Rajamani and another etc., dated 06.03.2025, it is held that, The executing court must dispose of the execution proceedings within six months from the date of filing, which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay. In view of above said judgment, the decree holder has not taken effective steps. There are no grounds to proceed further. Hence, this petition is dismissed for default and non prosecution.

hearings.business_text: The learned counsels for the Decree holder and the Judgment debtor are present. The learned counsel for the Judgment debtor filed memo stating that the Decree holder has not filed memo of calculations even after the Judgment debtor has vacated the petition schedule property on 07.08.2025. The Judgment debtor is ready to pay some part immediately once the Decree holder filed memo of calculations. Perused the memo and heard. It appears that the decree is for eviction of the Judgment debtor from the suit schedule property, arrears of rent of Rs.1,22,024/- and rent enhanced at the rate as agreed in Ex.P2 from the date of termination of tenancy i.e., 30.09.2023 till delivery of vacant possession of suit schedule property to the plaintiff as damages. The arrears of rent is already adjusted by this court by Judgment and Decree dated 14.06.2024. In the claim petition, the Decree holder has calculated the decree amount and mentioned the total amount payable by the Judgment debtor to the Decree holder. Therefore, it appears that filing the memo seeking memo of calculation from the Decree holder by the Judgment debtor is to drag on the proceedings. Hence, the memo filed by the Judgment debtor is hereby dismissed. The Judgment debtor has not paid the claim amount. Hence, for step against Judgment debtor. Call on 28.11.2025.

hearings.business_text: Orders on objection of JDR No.2 to the Execution Petition The JDR No.2 filed the statement of objections stating the facts of land acquisition, filing of writ petitions and also package compensation awarded by the JDR No.2 and with the specific contention that the JDR No.2 deposited the compensation amount before the JDR No.1. Hence, the JDR No.2 is not liable to pay any interest on the compensation amount and if at all there were any such liability that is on the JDR No.1 and accordingly, prayed for dismissal of execution petition. The DHR is filed this execution petition to enforce the judgment and award passed in LAC 104/2022 C/w LAC 106/2022. On the basis above points for consideration is that “whether the objections of JDR No. 2 is sustainable under law. ” Heard the arguments. Perused the material on record, on that basis my finding on the above point is in Negative for the following: REASONS This execution petition filed by the DHR to enforce the Judgment and Award passed in LAC 104/2022 C/w LAC 106/2022. In the said judgment the court awarded the interest on the basis of the facts of said case. The Judgment and Award passed by this court is a appealable order. There is no material on record to show that the JDR No.2 has challenged the said judgment till this date. Unless and until the judgment and award has been set aside or modified, the said judgment and award is binding on the parties. In the case on hand, the JDR No.2 only claimed that it is not responsible for the payment of interest. It is also relevant to note that the interest ordered in the award on the basis of non depositing of the compensation amount within the statutory prescribed time. If the JDRs aggrieved by the order then they have to challenge the said order otherwise the said judgment and decree binding on them. At this juncture it is also relevant to note that this court while passing the judgment specifically ordered that the claimant shall have to execute the indemnity bond with one surety in each case, undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or any other court if ordered to do so, which amount is going to receive in this case. Therefore, even if the JDR No.1 succeeds in the appeal filed by it, no prejudice will be caused to the JDRs as the amount released in favour of the DHR can be recovered either from the DHR or from the surety. Further, if at all the JDR No.2 already deposited amount before the JDR No.1, then certainly JDR No.1 is liable to pay the interest. In view of these facts, certainly the objections of the JDR is not sustainable and the said objections are almost similar to the objection raised in the land acquisition case. Therefore, this court is of the humble opinion that the objection of JDR No.2 is not sustainable and accordingly, the above point is answered in Negative . In the result following: ORDER Objection filed by JDR no.2 is overruled. Claimant and his advocate present. He has already produced his Aadhar card, PAN card and pass book with voucher. Smt. P. Sindhura Reddy W/o P.V. Subbareddy offer surety for claimant. hearings.business_text: Orders on IA No.3. IA No.3 filed by the JDR U/O 21 R 26 of CPC praying to stay the further proceedings of this case. The said application is supported with detailed affidavit of SLAO – Sri. N. Tejas Kumar. The DHR filed detailed objection to said application. On the basis of above, point for consideration is that “ Whether the JDR made out sufficient grounds to stay further proceedings of this case ? ’’ Heard the arguments. Perused the material on record, on that basis my finding on the above point is in Negative for the following: Reasons The present application filed by JDR U/O 21 R 26 of CPC which speaks about when court may stay execution. As per the said provision, when the Decree Holder filed a petition for enforcement of the decree and at that time if the Judgment Debtor shows a sufficient cause, the court may stay the execution of such decree for a reasonable time to enable the Judgment Debtor to apply the court having appellate jurisdiction in respect of the decree or the execution thereof for an order to get the stay of the execution of decree passed. Hence, as per the said provision, further proceedings can be stayed in order to facilitate reasonable time to the Judgment Debtor to approach the appellate court to challenge the decree and obtain the stay. The Decree Holder in this case filed this execution petition on 05-12-2024 to enforce the Judgment passed by this court dated 15-03-2024. Therefore, this execution petition is filed much after the lapse of appeal period. Further, after the filing this execution petition, the court caused cause notice to the JDRs that has been duly served on both the JDRs and they have appeared through their advocates before the court. Subsequently, this court issued a prohibitory order and call for the decree amount vide order dated 03-03-2025, subsequently when the Garnishee of JDR No.1 deposited the amount to the court, the JDR filed the present IA No.3 as on 15-03-2025. Since then more than a month time is lapsed which is sufficient for the JDRs to approach the appellate court and challenge the judgment and award passed by this court in LAC 104/2022 C/w LAC 106/2022 dated 15-03-2024 and get the stay of the operation of said judgment . Therefore, even after the lapse of one year from date of passing of judgment, this Judgment Debtor has not obtained any stay of further proceedings of this case from the appellate court. It is also relevant to note that, this court while passing the judgment dated 15-03-2024 itself awarded the interest on the compensation amount which is within the knowledge of JDRs. Further, it is well settled Principle of law that mere filing of the appeal itself is not a ground to stay further proceedings of this case. In view of the said facts, it is clear that JDR failed to make out sufficient grounds to stay further proceedings of this case. Hence, the following: ORDER The IA No. 3 is hereby dismissed. For orders on objection to execution petition by 02-05-2025.

hearings.business_text: Orders on objection of JDR No.2 to the Execution Petition The JDR No.2 filed the statement of objections stating the facts of land acquisition, filing of writ petitions and also package compensation awarded by the JDR No.2 and with the specific contention that the JDR No.2 deposited the compensation amount before the JDR No.1. Hence, the JDR No.2 is not liable to pay any interest on the compensation amount and if at all there were any such liability that is on the JDR No.1 and accordingly, prayed for dismissal of execution petition. The DHR is filed this execution petition to enforce the judgment and award passed in LAC 104/2022 C/w LAC 106/2022. On the basis above points for consideration is that “whether the objections of JDR No. 2 is sustainable under law. ” Heard the arguments. Perused the material on record, on that basis my finding on the above point is in Negative for the following: REASONS This execution petition filed by the DHR to enforce the Judgment and Award passed in LAC 104/2022 C/w LAC 106/2022. In the said judgment the court awarded the interest on the basis of the facts of said case. The Judgment and Award passed by this court is a appealable order. There is no material on record to show that the JDR No.2 has challenged the said judgment till this date. Unless and until the judgment and award has been set aside or modified, the said judgment and award is binding on the parties. In the case on hand, the JDR No.2 only claimed that it is not responsible for the payment of interest. It is also relevant to note that the interest ordered in the award on the basis of non depositing of the compensation amount within the statutory prescribed time. If the JDRs aggrieved by the order then they have to challenge the said order otherwise the said judgment and decree binding on them. At this juncture it is also relevant to note that this court while passing the judgment specifically ordered that the claimant shall have to execute the indemnity bond with one surety in each case, undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or any other court if ordered to do so, which amount is going to receive in this case. Therefore, even if the JDR No.1 succeeds in the appeal filed by it, no prejudice will be caused to the JDRs as the amount released in favour of the DHR can be recovered either from the DHR or from the surety. Further, if at all the JDR No.2 already deposited amount before the JDR No.1, then certainly JDR No.1 is liable to pay the interest. In view of these facts, certainly the objections of the JDR is not sustainable and the said objections are almost similar to the objection raised in the land acquisition case. Therefore, this court is of the humble opinion that the objection of JDR No.2 is not sustainable and accordingly, the above point is answered in Negative . In the result following: ORDER Objection filed by JDR no.2 is overruled. Claimant and his advocate present. He has already produced his Aadhar card, PAN card and pass book with voucher. Smt. P. Sindhura Reddy W/o P.V. Subbareddy offer surety for claimant. She has already produced her Aadhar Card, Sale deed bearing site No.138, Old CMC Katha No.2150, Now bearing BBMP Katha No.3383/2150/138, formed in the layout called “CLASSIC ORCHARDS’ Phase-2, carved pit om Su/Mp/84, 85/1 and 86/1 Kothanur village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk, dated 14.12.2017, Khata certificate, Tax paid receipt, EC, SBI loan Statement, property valuation statement, Affidavit of Surety accepted. hearings.judge: CCH17 II ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Orders on IA No.3. IA No.3 filed by the JDR U/O 21 R 26 of CPC praying to stay the further proceedings of this case. The said application is supported with detailed affidavit of SLAO – Sri. N. Tejas Kumar. The DHR filed detailed objection to said application. On the basis of above, point for consideration is that “ Whether the JDR made out sufficient grounds to stay further proceedings of this case ? ’’ Heard the arguments. Perused the material on record, on that basis my finding on the above point is in Negative for the following: Reasons The present application filed by JDR U/O 21 R 26 of CPC which speaks about when court may stay execution. As per the said provision, when the Decree Holder filed a petition for enforcement of the decree and at that time if the Judgment Debtor shows a sufficient cause, the court may stay the execution of such decree for a reasonable time to enable the Judgment Debtor to apply the court having appellate jurisdiction in respect of the decree or the execution thereof for an order to get the stay of the execution of decree passed. Hence, as per the said provision, further proceedings can be stayed in order to facilitate reasonable time to the Judgment Debtor to approach the appellate court to challenge the decree and obtain the stay. The Decree Holder in this case filed this execution petition on 05-12-2024 to enforce the Judgment passed by this court dated 15-03-2024. Therefore, this execution petition is filed much after the lapse of appeal period. Further, after the filing this execution petition, the court caused cause notice to the JDRs that has been duly served on both the JDRs and they have appeared through their advocates before the court. Subsequently, this court issued a prohibitory order and call for the decree amount vide order dated 03-03-2025, subsequently when the Garnishee of JDR No.1 deposited the amount to the court, the JDR filed the present IA No.3 as on 15-03-2025. Since then more than a month time is lapsed which is sufficient for the JDRs to approach the appellate court and challenge the judgment and award passed by this court in LAC 104/2022 C/w LAC 106/2022 dated 15-03-2024 and get the stay of the operation of said judgment . Therefore, even after the lapse of one year from date of passing of judgment, this Judgment Debtor has not obtained any stay of further proceedings of this case from the appellate court. It is also relevant to note that, this court while passing the judgment dated 15-03-2024 itself awarded the interest on the compensation amount which is within the knowledge of JDRs. Further, it is well settled Principle of law that mere filing of the appeal itself is not a ground to stay further proceedings of this case. In view of the said facts, it is clear that JDR failed to make out sufficient grounds to stay further proceedings of this case. Hence, the following: ORDER The IA No. 3 is hereby dismissed. For orders on objection to execution petition by 02-05-2025.
